conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Meeting  March 2 , 2021  5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Delaying In-Person Reopening to April 8 vs. Keeping March 15 Elementary Start Date
conflicts.summary: Following the failed Senate Bill 37 veto override, the board split 3-4 on whether to delay all in-person reopening until April 8, 2021 (after spring break) or proceed with the previously approved March 15 elementary reopening schedule.
conflicts.side_a_position: Delay in-person reopening for all schools until April 8, 2021 after spring break.
side_a_arguments: Provide teachers and staff additional time for COVID-19 vaccinations and second-dose protection before returning to classrooms.
Heal community division and give principals and families clear written answers on Plan B six-foot spacing and staff accommodations.
Align reopening with a post-spring-break transition rather than a mid-March disruption.
conflicts.side_b_position: Maintain the March 15, 2021 elementary reopening timeline.
side_b_arguments: First-dose vaccination studies showed strong partial protection (~92% cited) and local positivity rates had dropped from January peaks.
Students struggling academically and emotionally in remote instruction needed timely access to in-person learning options.
Staff accommodations for ADA and high COVID risk could cover the virtual teaching positions needed without delaying reopening.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to move reopening to April 8 failed 3-4 on roll call at 01:48:49, keeping the March 15 elementary reopening date in place.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Emergency Meeting  February 18, 2021  5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Adopting March 15 Elementary Reopening Timeline vs. Delaying for Full Staff Vaccination and SB 37 Action
conflicts.summary: Board members split 5-2 over whether to commit immediately to administration's March 15 elementary reopening schedule (and post-spring break secondary reopening) or delay reopening until educators received full two-dose vaccination immunity and Governor Cooper acted on Senate Bill 37.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt the March 15 elementary and post-spring-break secondary reopening timeline immediately regardless of SB 37's final status.
side_a_arguments: The board should take ownership of its reopening decision rather than deferring to state legislators or awaiting a potential veto.
Student mental health and learning struggles under prolonged Plan C required offering an in-person option for families who want it.
Initiating ~1,000 educator vaccinations per week alongside contact tracing, PPE, and school-closure protocols provided sufficient mitigation.
conflicts.side_b_position: Delay reopening or make the March 15 date contingent on SB 37 becoming law to allow full vaccination and a cleaner academic break.
side_b_arguments: Community positivity remained near 7-8% (above the board's 4% metric) with emerging variants, and educators were weeks away from full two-dose protection.
March 15 was driven by General Assembly SB 37 deadlines rather than a natural academic quarter break.
Waiting a week or tying the timeline to a gubernatorial veto would allow teacher feedback and a more logical calendar date.
conflicts.resolution: Dr. Mike Lee's motion adopting the March 15 elementary / post-spring-break secondary reopening timeline passed 5-2 by roll call at 02:07:01.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session  December 10, 2020  5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: EOC and CTE Exam Grading Scale Floor (80-100 vs. 90-100)
conflicts.summary: Board members split 4-3 over whether to amend the proposed 80-to-100 pandemic grading scale floor for state-mandated EOC and CTE exams to 90-to-100, and then voted 6-1 to adopt the 90-to-100 scale.
conflicts.side_a_position: Raise the minimum exam score floor to 90-to-100 to give students maximum grade protection during remote pandemic learning and encourage families who feel unsafe testing in person to postpone.
side_a_arguments: Pandemic learning disruptions are unprecedented and students deserve the strongest possible protection on exams weighted at 20% of course grades.
With a 90-to-100 scale, students who postpone testing with an incomplete until spring will not be penalized academically for prioritizing safety.
conflicts.side_b_position: Keep the floor at 80-to-100 to preserve a two-letter-grade range (A and B) and avoid the optics of a single-grade scale.
side_b_arguments: A 90-to-100 scale leaves only a single letter grade (A), creating poor optics compared to an 80-to-100 range with As and Bs.
An 80-to-100 floor already substantially mitigates potential grade loss for students who postpone testing until spring.
conflicts.resolution: The amendment to adopt a 90-to-100 scale passed 4-3, and the final amended motion passed 6-1 with only Dr. Mike Lee voting no.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session  December 10, 2020  5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Reconsideration of Reopening High School Athletics During COVID-19 Surge
conflicts.summary: Following a reconsideration motion by Dr. Mike Lee, the board split 4-3 to approve reopening basketball, cheerleading, and preseason workouts for soccer, lacrosse, and football despite rising county COVID-19 transmission.
conflicts.side_a_position: Reopen approved winter sports and spring preseason workouts under strict masking, screening, and no-spectator protocols so student-athletes do not lose scholarships, mental health, or multiple seasons.
side_a_arguments: Overwhelming emails from families and direct outreach from high school principals urged restoring athletic opportunities, noting neighboring districts were already playing.
Losing senior or consecutive seasons harms student-athletes' mental health and college recruiting prospects, especially for students of color.
Participation is voluntary for families and governed by mandatory masking during play, parent safety meetings, and health department tracking.
conflicts.side_b_position: Keep sports paused while community COVID-19 rates are worse than in November and students remain out of classrooms under Plan C.
side_b_arguments: Durham's COVID-19 metrics (6.3% positivity, 29.89 cases per 100,000) are substantially worse than when the board rejected athletics on November 19.
Indoor close-contact basketball poses high transmission risk and contradicts asking families to sacrifice holiday gatherings and keeping classrooms closed.
Reopening sports privileges athletics while arts, culinary, and hands-on CTE students remain deprived of in-person workshops.
conflicts.resolution: The motion to reopen basketball, cheerleading, and preseason workouts for soccer, lacrosse, and football passed 4-3.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting  November 19, 2020  6:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Reopening Winter and Contact High School Athletics
conflicts.summary: Board members split 3-4 on whether to approve starting winter basketball, cheerleading, field hockey, and off-season workouts for lacrosse, soccer, and football.
conflicts.side_a_position: Allow voluntary student-athlete participation under NCHSAA safety protocols and parent waivers to support student mental health, academic motivation, and athletic development.
side_a_arguments: Following NCHSAA guidelines, screenings, and parent risk disclosures provides transparency and choice for families.
Athletics motivate academic engagement and provide college pathway opportunities.
conflicts.side_b_position: Reject expanding high school athletics while indoor gathering limits are restricted and in-person classroom instruction remains closed.
side_b_arguments: Indoor contact sports conflict with Durham's 10-person gathering limit and ongoing COVID-19 spread.
Opening sports while classrooms remain closed sends troubling optics and raises safety and liability concerns.
conflicts.resolution: The motion to approve the athletics reopening plan failed 3-4.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session November 5, 2020  5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Duke ABC Science Collaborative Symptom-Screening App MOU vs. Independent Service App
conflicts.summary: The board split 4-3 to approve an emergency MOU with the Duke ABC Science Collaborative for a COVID-19 symptom-screening app after sharp debate over research ties, short notice, and alternative local apps.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the vetted Duke ABC Science Collaborative MOU immediately so staff and learning center families can begin training on a free, FERPA-compliant symptom checker owned by DPS.
side_a_arguments: DPS retains ownership of all student data, researchers cannot access data without DPS direction, and families must separately opt in and sign parental consent for research.
Duke IRB oversight and legal vetting by Tanya Giovanni and Dr. Julie Spencer provide stronger data protection than commercial vendors, and Dr. Sendak's alternative app carried added cost.
Learning centers and staff need the screening tool next week ahead of potential Plan B reopening.
conflicts.side_b_position: Table or delay the emergency MOU to allow public review, community trust-building, and exploration of an independent service-oriented app (such as Greenlight Ed / Dr. Mark Sendak's team) or joint collaboration.
side_b_arguments: The MOU was added at the last minute without being posted in the public packet or reviewed with families.
Deploying an app built by a medical research team triggers legitimate historical distrust in communities of color and Latinx communities, where ABC webinars had limited public access.

Greenlight Ed / Dr. Sendak's Pandemic Response Network team is already used at Student U and a Durham charter school, partners with community health workers, and is not tied to an active research study.
conflicts.resolution: The motion to approve the ABC Science Collaborative MOU passed 4-3.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting October 22,  2020  6:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Reopening High School Athletics (Volleyball and Cross Country) During Virtual Plan C Instruction
conflicts.summary: The board voted 5-2 to reopen cross country and volleyball without spectators under NCHSAA protocols over objections from two members regarding COVID-19 risk, liability waivers, and opening sports while classrooms remain closed.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve reopening cross country and volleyball with no spectators, transparent risk communication, and strict NCHSAA mitigation protocols as an optional opportunity for students.
side_a_arguments: Cross country and volleyball are lower-risk sports with extensive screening, facility cleaning, and medical return-to-play safeguards.
Participation is voluntary for parents and students, and requiring face masks during competition further minimizes risk.
Sports support students' social-emotional well-being during remote learning.
conflicts.side_b_position: Keep athletics closed while school buildings remain closed under Plan C due to district-sanctioned COVID-19 risk, waiver concerns, and conflicting optics.
side_b_arguments: Sanctioning extracurricular athletics while keeping classroom instruction virtual sends mixed messages like reopening bars before schools.
District legal liability and asking parents to sign waivers raise unresolved concerns when indoor volleyball carries aerosol risk.
conflicts.resolution: The motion to approve the athletics reopening plan starting with cross country and volleyball passed 5-2.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/24/22
conflicts.issue: Effective Date for Shifting from Mask Mandate to Mask-Recommended (April 4 vs. April 11, 2022)
conflicts.summary: Board members agreed that declining COVID-19 metrics and low CDC community transmission warranted moving toward mask-recommended after spring break, but split evenly 3-3 on beginning April 4 before passing an April 11 start date 4-2.
conflicts.side_a_position: Lift the indoor mask mandate to mask-recommended on Monday, April 4, 2022 immediately after spring break.
side_a_arguments: Durham had reached the CDC 'low' transmission level and both the city and county had lifted indoor mask mandates.
Spring break already gave families a week to prepare, and the board could use its scheduled April 7 meeting to reinstate masks if metrics worsened.
conflicts.side_b_position: Delay the transition to mask-recommended until Monday, April 11, 2022, one week after spring break.
side_b_arguments: Teachers, nurses, and school staff would be on spring break and needed non-break workdays to verify KN95/clear mask inventory, arrange classroom accommodations, and brief the board on April 7 on keeping classrooms open.
Waiting one week after spring break would help detect any post-travel BA.2 Omicron spikes before removing the mandate.
conflicts.resolution: The April 4 motion failed 3-3; Matt Sears then joined Natalie Beyer, Alexandra Valladares, and Bettina Umstead to approve the April 11 effective date 4-2 (with Frederick Xavier Ravin III and Jovonia Lewis voting No and Dr. Mike Lee absent).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting  November 19, 2020  6:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Plan B Second-Semester Reopening Framework, Opt-In Default, and <4% Positivity Threshold
conflicts.summary: The board divided over whether to defer approval of Plan B for continued community planning or authorize January 21/25 planning under an opt-in model gated by a sustained <4% COVID-19 positivity threshold.
conflicts.side_a_position: Authorize administration to plan toward a January 21/25 second-semester Plan B reopening under an opt-in default, contingent on county positivity remaining below 4% for at least two consecutive weeks.
side_a_arguments: Staff need a target date and operational authorization now to hire, schedule, and prepare logistics if conditions improve.
Switching to an opt-in model keeps Plan C as the default for most families while reserving limited in-person seats for vulnerable and EC students who need them.
Requiring two consecutive weeks below 4% positivity ensures the district will not reopen during a surge.
conflicts.side_b_position: Do not approve a target date or metric-triggered Plan B yet; prioritize multilingual outreach, community input, and wait until infection curves actually decline.
side_b_arguments: Community COVID-19 infection curves are surging, making it premature to commit to a specific reopening date or fixed percentage threshold.
Board materials and Plan B details have not yet been fully translated and communicated across all languages spoken by DPS families.
Staffing risks and the lack of clear cost-benefit justification for hybrid instruction require further refinement before board approval.
conflicts.resolution: Matt Sears's deferral motion was announced as failed by Chair Umstead; Dr. Mike Lee's motion incorporating Frederick Xavier Ravin III's opt-in and <4% positivity amendment passed on an announced 4-3 roll call vote (with Natalie Beyer having backed Sears's deferral motion and urged tabling, while the Chair announced 4-3).

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | Board of Education | Monthly Meeting | 2/24/22
conflicts.issue: Scheduling Action and Name Selection for Elementary School F (Pauli Murray vs. Betty Doretha Massenberg)
conflicts.summary: Board members split 5-2 over adding Elementary School F naming to the February 24 agenda without prior notice, and disagreed over whether to proceed immediately to a vote or defer action to a future meeting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Bring Elementary School F naming back immediately for board discussion and potential decision, favoring Betty Doretha Massenberg (or Murray-Massenberg).
side_a_arguments: The naming item had already appeared on October 21, November 18, and December 9 agendas, and community due diligence and public advocacy for Betty Doretha Massenberg were complete.
Deferring repeatedly without explanation left the community waiting to give the new school its identity.
conflicts.side_b_position: Restrict the unscheduled agenda addition to discussion only and defer any final vote to a noticed March or April meeting.
side_b_arguments: Board members and staff had not been informed ahead of time that the naming item would be brought up, leaving unreadiness for an immediate vote.
Because the item was added only for discussion, taking action without amending the agenda again would be procedurally improper.
conflicts.resolution: The board voted 5-2 to add the item for discussion only, heard remarks from Ravin, Valladares, Lewis, and Chip Suddeth, and deferred a formal vote to a March or April agenda.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session November 5, 2020  5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Advancing Teacher Crowdfunding Policy (7360/85) on First Reading Without Teacher Input
conflicts.summary: The board split 6-1 on advancing first-reading cleanup policies that included a new policy requiring principal approval for teacher crowdfunding campaigns up to $5,000 and superintendent approval up to $25,000.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the cleanup policy batch including Policy 7360/85 on first reading to promote equity, asset accountability, and visibility into unmet classroom needs, while collecting teacher feedback before or after second reading.
side_a_arguments: The $5,000 principal and $25,000 superintendent thresholds are high enough to avoid burdening routine classroom campaigns.
Tracking crowdfunding helps the district identify unmet school needs and establish clear property ownership rules.
conflicts.side_b_position: Pull the crowdfunding policy before advancing so teachers can review and provide input on how principal-permission rules affect their practice.
side_b_arguments: Durham teachers frequently rely on crowdfunding and a teacher already messaged asking to give feedback.
Requiring principal sign-off even for small $100 music or classroom requests represents a major procedural shift that warrants teacher engagement first.
conflicts.resolution: The motion to advance the cleanup policies to second reading passed 6-1 with Natalie Beyer voting no.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting September 24,  2020  6:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Duration of Plan C Remote Learning Extension (Full Second Quarter vs. Four-Week Phased Review)
conflicts.summary: The board voted 6-1 to stay in Plan C through the second nine weeks, with Jovonia Lewis dissenting in favor of a shorter four-week extension and a phased-in Plan B option for Exceptional Children and K-2 students prior to January.
conflicts.side_a_position: Remain in remote Plan C for the entire second nine weeks (first semester) while continuing to build safety plans, Ignite capacity, and teacher readiness for a possible January Plan B.
side_a_arguments: Teachers and families need predictability and adequate preparation time rather than mid-quarter schedule disruptions.
With roughly 20% of teachers expressing readiness and rising second-wave risks, large districts should be observed before transitioning.
The board retains authority to revisit phasing in smaller high-need groups if conditions and plans mature.
conflicts.side_b_position: Limit the Plan C extension to four weeks (after the initial nine weeks) and develop an earlier phased-in Plan B option in November for EC self-contained and K-2 students.
side_b_arguments: A blanket second-quarter Plan C commitment leaves behind the most vulnerable students, particularly EC self-contained and early elementary learners.
A four-week checkpoint would force rapid development of psychological safety and small-group in-person options before January.
conflicts.resolution: The motion to remain in Plan C for the second nine weeks passed 6-1 with Jovonia Lewis voting no.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session September 10,  2020  5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Adding a Title I Federal Funding Update to the Approved Agenda
conflicts.summary: The board voted 6-1 to amend its already-approved agenda to hear an immediate 10-minute presentation on Title I school funding allocations, with Dr. Mike Lee voting no.
conflicts.side_a_position: Amend the agenda immediately to provide a public Title I funding update so families and community members can understand how federal Title I dollars are distributed across DPS schools.
side_a_arguments: Community members frequently ask how federal Title I funds are allocated to schools.
Presenting the Title I plan publicly increases transparency rather than leaving it solely on consent.
conflicts.side_b_position: Decline to amend the already-approved agenda mid-meeting.
side_b_arguments: Voted no during the procedural roll call after the agenda and consent items had already been adopted.
conflicts.resolution: The motion passed 6-1 and Dr. Hardy and Dr. Danner delivered the Title I update.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Budget Hearing & Work Session | 4/7/22
conflicts.issue: Approval of April 7, 2022 Personnel Report
conflicts.summary: Following closed session, the board split 5-1 on approving the April 7, 2022 personnel report, with Dr. Mike Lee casting the sole dissenting vote.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the April 7, 2022 personnel report as presented following closed session.
side_a_arguments: Five board members voted in favor following closed-session review (specific personnel rationale discussed in closed session).
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose approval of the April 7, 2022 personnel report.
side_b_arguments: Dr. Mike Lee voted No during the open-session roll call without stating an open-session explanation.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 5-1 on roll call (Jovonia Lewis not recorded).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 12, 2021 5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Cafeteria Reopening vs. Prioritizing Outdoor Lunch and Amending Reopening Motion Language
conflicts.summary: During review of the 2021-22 COVID-19 reopening plan, board members diverged on how strongly to mandate or prioritize outdoor dining over indoor cafeterias and whether to formally amend staff's cafeteria recommendation slide before voting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Prioritize outdoor eating with tents/shade and explicitly move outdoor-meal language ahead of indoor cafeteria reinstatement in the board's approved recommendations.
side_a_arguments: Unmasked indoor eating in crowded cafeterias poses heightened Delta-variant transmission risk for unvaccinated K-6 students.
Leading the recommendation slide with reinstating cafeterias sends the wrong signal to families and principals unless outdoor options are emphasized first or formally amended.
conflicts.side_b_position: Preserve principal/school-site flexibility across cafeterias, classrooms, and outdoor spaces without requiring outdoor lunch in harsh weather or amending the recommendation text.
side_b_arguments: Not every child is comfortable eating outdoors during extreme summer heat, rain, or freezing winter weather, and accommodations are needed for indoor options.
Not all school campuses or facilities can immediately accommodate full outdoor dining, and the recommendation already encourages outdoor space weather permitting.
conflicts.resolution: After administration confirmed schools already had flexibility across cafeterias, classrooms, and outdoors—and noted DPS Foundation grants were funding outdoor tents—the board agreed to proceed with the unamended motion while committing to support principals with outdoor learning and eating resources, passing the plan 6-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session November 4, 2021 5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Board Redistricting Map Selection: Member-Drawn Option E vs. Consultant-Drawn Option C
conflicts.summary: Board members and public commenters divided over whether to advance Option E, crafted by Board Member Frederick Xavier Ravin III to account for future growth, or select consultant-drawn Option C ahead of Board of Elections deadlines.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support Option E's aggressive accommodation of population growth trends across Districts 2, 3, and 4 so the board does not have to revisit maps prematurely.
side_a_arguments: Following growth data and demographic trends avoids rapid imbalances before the next census.
Option E passed legal thresholds while incorporating local insight into fast-growing areas.
conflicts.side_b_position: Adopt consultant-drawn Option C to preserve community trust in independent redistricting experts, meet election deadlines, and avoid divisive optics.
side_b_arguments: Independent consultants followed the board's adopted criteria and produced well-thought-out maps such as Option C.
Public feedback on Option E was sharply divisive, whereas Option C commands unifying support and satisfies election timing.
conflicts.resolution: Dr. Mike Lee affirmed Ravin's good-faith intentions while moving adoption of Map C (Option C), seconded by Bettina Umstead, which passed 7-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting June 24, 2021 6:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Outsourcing Substitute Teacher Staffing to Kelly Education Services
conflicts.summary: Administration proposed contracting substitute teacher management to third-party vendor Kelly Education Services to improve low fill rates and offer weekly pay and ACA benefit options, while multiple board members pushed back sharply over privatization precedents, vendor markup and benefit quality, and missing stakeholder consultation.
conflicts.side_a_position: Partner with Kelly Education Services under a 30-day evergreen contract to provide weekly pay, 5-day workweeks, ACA benefits, and dedicated placement support for substitutes.
side_a_arguments: Substitute fill rates fell to 68% in 2019-21 (75% five-year average), disrupting classrooms and forcing teachers and principals to cover uncovered classes.
State health plan and ACA/retiree rules bar DPS from offering standard state benefits or weekly payroll to non-permanent substitutes without costly HR/payroll staffing and Serenic software changes.
Kelly charges no upfront fee, projects $80,000-$100,000 in district savings, preserves DPS's $15+/hour pay rate, and could raise fill rates toward 95%.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defer action on outsourcing and examine in-house alternatives, full labor/cost analysis, and direct input from substitutes, teachers, and principals before privatizing substitute positions.
side_b_arguments: The board recently went through a difficult process bringing custodial staff back in-house and is wary of setting a precedent for privatizing public school roles or relying on a vendor's 1.3x markup and inferior private health plans.

No actual contract was included in the packet, and staff had not quantified central-office/treasurer labor savings or explored hiring a smaller 50-75 full-time internal sub pool or contracting out biweekly payroll alone.
The board needed direct feedback from classroom teachers, principals, and current substitutes before changing their employment status.
conflicts.resolution: Seeing strong board unreadiness and unanswered questions, HR Chief Dr. Alvera Lesane agreed to pause the proposal and convene stakeholder sessions with teachers, principals, and substitutes before bringing it back to the board.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOCC/BOE Quarterly Meeting May 18, 2021 9:00 AM
conflicts.issue: DPS Budget Request Submission Deadline (April 1 vs. Mid-March) in Joint MOU
conflicts.summary: DPS MOU drafters proposed moving the school board's annual draft budget request to the county from mid-March to April 1, while County Budget Director Keith Lane urged keeping the mid-March timeline.
conflicts.side_a_position: Move the DPS draft budget request deadline in the joint MOU from mid-March to April 1.
side_a_arguments: Aligns the school district's budget preparation with the county's budget development cycle.
conflicts.side_b_position: Retain the mid-March deadline for DPS's initial budget request.
side_b_arguments: DPS funding is by far the county's largest budget allocation, and April 1 arrives after all other county department requests are already being compiled.
Moving two weeks later prevents county budget staff from comparing DPS needs alongside other county departments.
conflicts.resolution: After County Budget Director Keith Lane raised the timing concern, Chair Bettina Umstead agreed to amend the draft MOU back to the earlier mid-March date pending sign-off by Jovonia Lewis and Frederick Xavier Ravin III ahead of the next quarterly meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: BOCC/BOE Joint Quarterly Meeting | May 10, 2022 | 9:00AM
conflicts.issue: FY23 County Funding Level for DPS ($9.88M Recommended vs. $12.875M Ask, Classified Wages, and School Nurse Funding)
conflicts.summary: DPS board members and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga pressed County leaders for greater funding beyond the County Manager's $9.88 million recommended increase to address classified wages ($16-$17/hour), teacher supplement competition, and school nurse funds, while County officials cited tax impacts and existing nurse vacancies.
conflicts.side_a_position: Increase local funding toward DPS's full ask, raise classified staff from $15/hr toward $16-$17/hr, and direct school nurse funds to address classroom/staffing needs.
side_a_arguments: DPS faces intense regional competition on teacher salary supplements and severe classified vacancies at the $15/hour wage floor (~$4M needed to reach $16-$17/hr).
Roughly $1.1 million funded previously for school health nurses stayed in County Public Health rather than coming directly to DPS.
Both boards need a multi-year funding plan and joint advocacy for state Leandro funding from the state's $6 billion rainy day fund.
conflicts.side_b_position: Hold the recommended FY23 DPS increase at $9.88 million (8.97% general fund growth) and avoid additional property tax hikes while filling existing vacancies.
side_b_arguments: The $9.88 million increase matches general fund revenue growth and covers $5.3 million in state salary/benefit pass-throughs, plus mid-year nurse funding commitment once 10 existing vacancies are filled.
Residents already face inflation at the grocery store and an upcoming 2.5-cent tax impact if the 2022 school bond passes.
State lawmakers—who refused local school board taxing authority—must fund public education rather than relying solely on local property taxes.
conflicts.resolution: Informational joint budget discussion; no formal funding vote taken at the joint meeting.

conflicts.issue: Transition to Mask-Recommended Policy Effective April 4, 2022
conflicts.summary: Jovonia Lewis moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded moving DPS to mask-recommended starting April 4, 2022 immediately upon return from spring break. Chair Bettina Umstead asked to amend the date to April 11 to give staff and nurses time after break to prepare PPE, classroom spacing, and an April 7 update on keeping classrooms open, but under board procedure the original motion proceeded to a roll call vote and failed on a 3-3 tie.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 3-3)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (3-3)

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education | Work Session | 3/10/22
conflicts.issue: Adding Unnoticed Mask Mandate Vote to Work Session and Timing of Indoor Mandate Vote
conflicts.summary: Board members debated both the procedural propriety of adding an unnoticed mask mandate vote to a work session agenda and whether to vote immediately on renewing the indoor mandate rather than waiting for the March 24 regular meeting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Add the mask mandate vote to the work session agenda and act on both outdoor recommendations and renewing the indoor mandate.
side_a_arguments: Major shifts had occurred since the February 24 vote, including Durham City and County lifting mandates and updated CDC guidance.
Renewing the indoor mandate during the March 10 session would satisfy the monthly statutory requirement for March.
conflicts.side_b_position: Avoid surprising staff without advance materials and defer any indoor mask mandate vote until the regularly noticed March 24 meeting.
side_b_arguments: Best governance practice is giving the superintendent, staff, fellow board members, and community advance notice and background materials before agenda votes.
Community members did not expect an indoor mask mandate decision at a work session and should have full notice ahead of March 24.
conflicts.resolution: The board approved adding Item 9B and voted 7-0 to adopt outdoor masking relaxation effective March 16, while Frederick Xavier Ravin III withdrew his motion to renew the indoor mandate so it would be taken up on March 24.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education | Work Session | 3/10/22
conflicts.issue: Timeline for Classified Staff Pay Adjustments ($17/hr Now vs. December 2022 Compensation Study)
conflicts.summary: Administration proposed waiting for a comprehensive classification and compensation study finishing in December 2022 for FY 2023-24 implementation, whereas board members argued classified employees needed immediate FY 2022-23 wage action.
conflicts.side_a_position: Accelerate raising remaining classified staff to $17/hour in the FY 2022-23 budget request rather than waiting for the 2023-24 cycle.
side_a_arguments: Raising bus drivers to $17/hour left instructional assistants and other classified staff behind despite severe inflation and labor market competition.
Durham County added $20 million to its fund balance and instructional assistants would not wait until December 2022 or 2023-24 without retroactive pay.
conflicts.side_b_position: Use the RFP compensation study through December 2022 to build a comprehensive, sustainable pay structure for FY 2023-24 while prioritizing across-the-board teacher supplements in FY 2022-23.
side_b_arguments: A thorough internal and external vendor comparison across certified, classified, and central office roles takes until December 2022 and avoids piecemeal fixes.
Adding immediate $17/hour classified increases would expand the FY 2022-23 local budget request from ~$12.8 million to ~$17.2 million.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Superintendent Dr. Mubenga confirmed finance staff already had the $3.7-$4.4 million cost ready to include in the FY 2022-23 budget proposal if directed by the board.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Public Hearing October 21, 2021 5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Consideration of Board-Member-Drawn Redistricting Map (Option E) vs. Consultant-Drawn Maps
conflicts.summary: Public commenters and board members clashed over the legitimacy and merits of Option E, drawn by sitting Board Member Frederick Xavier Ravin III outside the independent consultant process, versus consultant-crafted Options B, C, and D.
conflicts.side_a_position: Include and consider Option E because it uses data trends to accommodate future East Durham population growth and keeps Districts 1 and 2 together as communities of interest.
side_a_arguments: Option E prioritizes accommodating rapid future population growth in fast-growing areas of Durham County.
Supporters argued Option E keeps Districts 1 and 2 as communities of interest together and challenges status-quo mapping.
conflicts.side_b_position: Reject Option E and choose exclusively from maps drawn by independent, neutral consultants to protect process integrity and compactness.
side_b_arguments: Sitting elected officials should not draw their own electoral districts, which creates the appearance of gerrymandering or self-dealing regardless of intent.

Expert analysis noted Option E emphasized growth over compactness and dispersed Black/African American population share slightly in consolidated districts; Chair Umstead also restricted Ravin from advocating for Option E during the expert/public hearing.
conflicts.resolution: No vote was taken at the public hearing; Chair Umstead closed the hearing at 00:49:02 and scheduled the final map vote for the November 4, 2021 work session.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session October 7, 2021 5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Conditioning Staff Retention Bonus on COVID-19 Vaccination/Testing Survey Compliance
conflicts.summary: Frederick Xavier Ravin III proposed tying the $1,000 retention bonus—or a vaccination incentive—to employees completing the COVID-19 vaccination/testing survey, while legal counsel and other board members urged keeping the bonus unconditional for morale and ESSER compliance.
conflicts.side_a_position: Use the bonus or an attached requirement to incentivize employees to report vaccination status or comply with district testing protocols.
side_a_arguments: Tying an incentive to filling out the vaccination/testing survey could increase staff compliance.
conflicts.side_b_position: Approve a clean, unconditional $1,000 retention bonus before the holidays and address vaccination incentives separately.
side_b_arguments: Legal counsel advised ESSER funds likely cannot be used for monetary vaccine incentives or non-retention bonuses.
Staff morale is strained by the pandemic, and mixing vaccination enforcement into the bonus would complicate and delay relief.
conflicts.resolution: The board approved Bettina Umstead's clean $1,000 retention bonus motion without vaccination or survey conditions.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting September 23, 2021 6:30 PM
conflicts.issue: Spark Scholars Virtual Program Magnet-Seat Retention and Edmentum Contract Approval
conflicts.summary: Board members debated whether students transferring from magnet schools into the one-year Spark Scholars virtual stopgap program should keep their magnet seats for the following year, and whether to separate the Edmentum contract vote from that programmatic rule. The contract passed 6-1 by voice vote.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the up-to-$825,000 Edmentum contract directly so Spark Scholars can launch promptly without delaying on magnet-seat rules, while honoring Ignite's advance commitment process.
side_a_arguments: Edmentum provides immediate virtual staffing stability for up to 300 waitlisted students given current teacher shortages.
Ignite Online Academy is the permanent pathway where families committed during the application window, whereas Spark Scholars is a one-year stopgap.
conflicts.side_b_position: Allow Spark Scholars families from magnet schools to retain their magnet seats without penalty—or address the programmatic rule alongside the contract—rather than forcing them back into the lottery.
side_b_arguments: Because Spark Scholars is explicitly a one-year temporary program during the Delta surge for medically fragile or immunocompromised families, magnet schools do not lose seats this year.
Letting the handful of families return to their magnet school community without penalty is fairer than requiring re-entry into the lottery.
conflicts.resolution: Dr. Mike Lee's standalone motion to approve the up-to-$825,000 Edmentum contract passed 6-1 by voice vote (with the lone dissenter and non-moving Aye voters not named in the voice vote).

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education | Work Session | 12/9/21
conflicts.issue: Enforcement of Staff COVID-19 Vaccination Mandate vs. Ongoing Weekly Testing
conflicts.summary: Board members challenged administration over allowing roughly 1,400 unvaccinated employees to remain compliant through weekly testing rather than enforcing a strict vaccination requirement, debating whether positive outreach and incentives or stricter accountability were needed.
conflicts.side_a_position: Clarify expectations and move beyond passive weekly testing because the district is effectively operating under a testing mandate rather than achieving its 100% vaccination mandate.
side_a_arguments: Allowing unvaccinated employees to simply test once a week undermines the board's stated vaccination mandate.
Roughly 1,400 employees remain unvaccinated, leaving students and families less safe and requiring concrete incentives and direct nurse outreach at job sites.
conflicts.side_b_position: Recognize operational staffing constraints and cultural hesitancy while continuing weekly testing, masking, and gradual outreach that lowered monthly staff cases.
side_b_arguments: Weekly mandatory testing, masking, and lunch protocols have helped reduce monthly staff positive cases from 60+ to roughly 20 out of 5,400+ employees.
Staffing shortages across schools and departments make sudden termination or harsher penalties operationally challenging while outreach continues.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the board directed administration to coordinate with the Durham County Health Department for on-site vaccine access/education and return in January with employee vaccination incentive options.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOE/BOCC Quarterly Meeting November 16, 2021 9:00 AM
conflicts.issue: Framing of Escalating DPS Capital Improvement Plan Costs ('Tidal Wave' vs. Deferred Needs)
conflicts.summary: County budget officials framed the jump in five-year CIP requests from $400M to over $1B as an unaffordable 'tidal wave' requiring scrutiny of shovel-readiness and LGC/rating-agency capacity, while Dr. Mike Lee objected to rhetoric implying DPS was inflating requests rather than addressing overdue deferred maintenance and construction inflation.
conflicts.side_a_position: Highlight the rapid expansion of CIP spending requests as a fiscal 'tidal wave' exceeding historical spend patterns and potentially beyond county affordability without strict prioritization.
side_a_arguments: Five-year CIP requests climbed from $400M two years ago to over $1B, with DPS's 5-year request jumping from $110M to $352M.
The Local Government Commission (LGC) and bond rating agencies will scrutinize debt authorizations compared to historical spend capacity.
conflicts.side_b_position: Reject narratives suggesting DPS is padding or mismanaging its capital budget, emphasizing that cost growth stems from inflation, state underfunding, and compounding deferred facility needs.
side_b_arguments: Deferring school repairs causes nonlinear, exponential future cost increases ('future cost of money').
The DPS facility master plan reflects genuine, professionally vetted district survival needs rather than 'pork' or discretionary add-ons.
conflicts.resolution: County Manager Claudia Hager clarified the chart also reflected K-12 state underfunding and county project growth ($719M non-DPS), and both boards committed to reviewing debt-capacity and tax scenarios together ahead of February 2022.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session September 9, 2021 5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Weekly Testing Opt-Out vs. Strict Exemptions Under Staff COVID-19 Vaccination Mandate
conflicts.summary: Ahead of passing the staff vaccine mandate, board members differed on whether unvaccinated employees without medical or religious exemptions should be permitted weekly testing as an alternative or face stricter consequences.
conflicts.side_a_position: Allow administrative discretion to require weekly testing for employees who decline vaccination.
side_a_arguments: Weekly testing provides a practical safeguard while accommodating administrative discretion on non-vaccinated staff.
conflicts.side_b_position: Reject testing as a general opt-out and limit testing accommodations strictly to approved religious or medical exemptions.
side_b_arguments: The mandate should send a clear, strong statement requiring full vaccination across all ~5,200 staff rather than functioning as a testing opt-out.
Exemption procedures should cover medical and religious exemptions, while administration returns with recommendations for outright refusals.
conflicts.resolution: The board unanimously approved Attorney Ken Soo's motion mandating full vaccination by October 31, 2021 and directing administration to return with implementation details on exemptions, appeals, and exempt-staff regular testing.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOCC/BOE Quarterly Meeting May 18, 2021 9:00 AM
conflicts.issue: Proposed Budget Indexing Formula in Joint BOCC/BOE MOU
conflicts.summary: Frederick Xavier Ravin III and the draft MOU proposed exploring a budget indexing formula for DPS funding, while another official cautioned against locking boards into a rigid formula without staff study.
conflicts.side_a_position: Establish a working indexing formula in the MOU to project expected school system funding needs.
side_a_arguments: Creates a more transparent and predictable budget development process for both boards and staff.
conflicts.side_b_position: Have mutual budget staffs thoroughly review or study any indexing formula for a year before adopting it.
side_b_arguments: Locking into a formula could prevent the boards from having deep, responsive discussions as community needs change.
conflicts.resolution: Deferred for joint budget staff review and feedback before finalizing the MOU at the next quarterly meeting.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/29/22
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its resumed monthly meeting on June 29, 2022, chaired by Bettina Umstead. After unanimously amending the agenda and voting to enter an extended closed session, the board returned to open session and passed a 7-0 roll-call vote to amend the agenda for an open-session personnel discussion. On a motion by Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded by Alexandra Valladares, the board then voted 7-0 to adopt the sixth amendment to Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's contract, extending his tenure for an additional year. Chair Umstead praised Dr. Mubenga's leadership during COVID-19 recovery, focus on student social-emotional needs, and educator advocacy, while Dr. Mubenga thanked the board and Durham community before adjournment.

agenda_items.title: Resumption of Meeting, Agenda Amendment, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead resumed the meeting from the prior agenda and called for a motion to amend the agenda to align with the updated agenda items. Following unanimous approval of the agenda amendment, Natalie Beyer moved and Alexandra Valladares seconded entering closed session, which passed unanimously by voice vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda amendment passed unanimously; Closed session passed unanimously

agenda_items.title: Return to Open Session and Agenda Amendment for Personnel Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from closed session after approximately 87 minutes, the board entertained a motion to amend the agenda to include an open-session discussion of personnel. Because board member Dr. Mike Lee was participating remotely via Zoom, Chair Umstead conducted a named roll-call vote, with all seven members voting in favor.

agenda_items.title: Sixth Amendment to Superintendent's Contract (One-Year Extension)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Frederick Xavier Ravin III moved and Alexandra Valladares seconded adopting the sixth amendment to Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's contract, extending his contract for an additional year, which passed 7-0 on a named roll-call vote. Chair Umstead commended Dr. Mubenga's focus on student social-emotional needs, academic learning gains, strategic planning, and educator advocacy through the COVID-19 pandemic, expressing hope for a state raise in the upcoming budget bill, and Dr. Mubenga expressed gratitude for the board's vote of confidence.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/23/22
meetings.executive_summary: The June 23, 2022 Durham Public Schools Board of Education monthly meeting opened with annual employee celebrations and farewell tributes honoring outgoing board members Dr. Mike Lee and Frederick Xavier Ravin III. In his update, Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga congratulated roughly 1,800 graduating seniors and clarified that Lakewood and Bethesda Elementary Schools are not magnet schools and their dual language immersion programs were not being treated as sunsetting magnet programs. After proposing to defer Item 11A (Community Safety and Wellness Task Force educator vacancy) so members could interview three newly received applicants (with middle items truncated in the transcript digest), the board conducted its second reading of the Growing Together plan and voted unanimously (7-0) to adopt the academic application programs and revised boundaries across 32 elementary schools targeting January 2024 implementation. Following a closed session, the board unanimously approved the June 23 personnel report (7-0) and voted 7-0 to recess until Wednesday at 5:30 p.m. for personnel.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Employee Celebrations, and Farewell Tributes for Outgoing Board Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the meeting to order and led a moment of silence. Staff recognized DPS educators and employees of the year, and board members delivered farewell tributes and presented plaques to outgoing members Dr. Mike Lee and Frederick Xavier Ravin III, highlighting Ravin's prior service on the Budget Advisory Committee and Special Needs Advisory Committee.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga celebrated approximately 1,800 DPS seniors graduating from specialty high schools and Cameron Indoor Stadium ceremonies. He also addressed community concerns regarding Lakewood and Bethesda Elementary Schools, clarifying they are not magnet schools and their dual language immersion programs are not sunsetting magnet programs.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Proposed Deferral of Item 11A (Community Safety and Wellness Task Force)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A motion was made to approve the agenda, followed by a motion to amend the agenda to defer Item 11A—filling the educator vacancy on the DPS Community Safety and Wellness Task Force—to the next meeting because three applications had arrived only two days earlier and board members needed time to speak with candidates. The vote outcome and subsequent middle agenda items were truncated in the digest.

agenda_items.title: Growing Together Plan: Second Reading and Final Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matthew Palmer, Dr. Benjamin, and Director Melody Marshall presented the second reading of the Growing Together plan covering 32 elementary schools, neighborhood base areas, lottery seats, year-round intersession enrichment, IB pathways, and dual language immersion ahead of Lyons Farm opening in August 2022 and full implementation in January 2024. Board members questioned staff on IB whole-school design, regional year-round access, transportation barriers, and whether action could be delayed, before Jovonia Lewis moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded final adoption, passing unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session, Personnel Report, and Recess to Wednesday
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session at 04:08:32. Returning to open session at 05:18:43, the board approved the June 23 personnel report unanimously (7-0) and voted unanimously (7-0) to recess the meeting until Wednesday at 5:30 p.m. for personnel matters.

meetings.executive_summary: During its June 9, 2022 work session, the Board of Education amended its agenda (7-0) at Natalie Beyer's request to add a resolution opposing North Carolina House Bill 755 (Parents' Bill of Rights) and approved the May 5 minutes (7-0) and consent agenda (7-0), including Item 6A for comprehensive door-access security systems at six high schools and one conversion site. Public commenters asked about school security protocols following the Uvalde, Texas shooting, requested support for Latina/o early childhood learners, commented on school Pride Month displays, and urged preservation of Lakewood Elementary's dual language immersion program. Board members began reading the HB 755 resolution citing existing parental rights and non-discrimination concerns before middle items were truncated in the digest. Later in the session, the board unanimously approved a revised gender-neutral, CROWN Act-aligned dress code policy on first reading (7-0) advancing to June 23, discussed hesitation around a Durham High Forever commemorative plaque request lacking an alumni-gift policy, and approved the June 9 personnel report (7-0) after closed session.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Five scheduled speakers plus walk-up commenters addressed the board under three-minute rules. agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-S)

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education | Public Hearing - Growing Together
meetings.executive_summary: The Board of Education held a dedicated public hearing on June 1, 2022 to receive community feedback on the Growing Together elementary boundary and academic program realignment plan. Lakewood Elementary parents, PTA leaders, and educators—including translated testimony from a Spanish-speaking mother—strongly urged the board to retain Lakewood's three-year-old Spanish dual language immersion (DLI) program, citing pandemic disruptions to the inaugural cohort, Lakewood's 51% native Spanish-speaking student body, and the absence of finalized legacy/grandfathering rules. Following public comment, Matthew Palmer outlined the multi-year implementation timeline leading up to the scheduled June vote and Lyons Farm's August 2022 opening. Board members including Dr. Mike Lee and Chair Bettina Umstead closed by balancing the urgency of addressing systemic district inequities without delaying until 2025-26 against requests for transparent legacy/grandfathering rules, transfer appeals, and transportation cost details; no formal votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Opening and Rules Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the Growing Together public hearing, introduced Spanish interpreters Martha Romo Aguiles and Marty Ramirez, and reviewed the three-minute public comment guidelines. She noted the Growing Together boundary and student assignment review had been underway for over two years.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Growing Together and Lakewood Elementary Dual Language Immersion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lakewood Elementary parents and community members—including Arden Ragsdale, Mike Silver, Karen Miller, PTA President Ali, Kristen Me, Jesse Bravermann, and Delaney Susie (reading translated remarks from a Spanish-speaking mother)—urged the board not to remove the three-year-old Spanish dual language immersion program from Lakewood. Speakers cited COVID-19 disruptions to the inaugural cohort, principal turnover, Lakewood's 51% native Spanish-speaking population, and the lack of concrete legacy/grandfathering commitments.

agenda_items.title: Growing Together Implementation Timeline Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At Chair Umstead's request, Matthew Palmer reviewed the multi-year Growing Together timeline leading toward second reading and board action in June, the opening of Lyons Farm Elementary in August 2022, and subsequent transition years. He acknowledged community comments regarding legacy/grandfathering policies and transportation.

agenda_items.title: Board Reflections on Equity, Grandfathering Rules, and Decision Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members including Dr. Mike Lee and Chair Bettina Umstead discussed the tension between ensuring timely resource equity—cautioning against pushing full implementation out to 2025-26—and providing families clear legacy/grandfathering options, transfer appeal processes, and transportation fiscal impacts ahead of the final vote. Chair Umstead emphasized multilingual parent outreach before adjourning at 01:58:28.

meetings.title: BOCC/BOE Joint Quarterly Meeting | May 10, 2022 | 9:00AM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead presided over the May 10, 2022 in-person joint quarterly meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners (BOCC) and DPS Board of Education, which unanimously approved the agenda and February 15, 2022 minutes. DPS Building Services Director Frederick Davis and Dr. Julius Monk presented construction progress videos on Lyons Farm Elementary (on schedule and budget for August 2022) and the 2,000-student Northern High School, prompting intergovernmental discussion of unfunded off-site pedestrian/sidewalk improvements and County ARPA broadband investments ($10 million set aside). County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell presented her recommended FY23 budget featuring a $9.88 million (8.97%) funding increase for DPS totaling $176 million. In extensive Q&A, school board members and Dr. Mubenga pressed for higher local funding to raise classified wages above $15/hour toward $16-$17/hour, questioned $1.1 million in unspent Public Health school nurse funding, and urged joint Leandro advocacy, while County Manager Sowell and commissioners cited existing nurse vacancies and resident property tax strain alongside the proposed 2.5-cent bond tax impact.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, and February 15, 2022 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the first in-person BOCC/BOE joint quarterly meeting in recent memory to order at 9:00 a.m. The joint boards unanimously approved the agenda by voice vote (seconded by Jovonia Lewis) and unanimously approved the February 15, 2022 joint meeting minutes (moved by BOCC Chair Howerton, seconded by Jovonia Lewis).

agenda_items.title: DPS Capital Projects Update: Lyons Farm Elementary and Northern High School
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk and Executive Director of Building Services Frederick Davis presented video recaps showing Lyons Farm Elementary on schedule and budget for August 2022 completion and structural/site progress at the new 2,000-student Northern High School. Officials discussed off-site sidewalk and American Tobacco Trail access needs not in the original project budget—recommending City of Durham participation—as well as $10 million in County ARPA broadband equity funds and state GREAT grants.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Recommended FY23 Budget Update and Joint Funding Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell outlined her recommended FY23 budget increasing DPS county funding by $9.88 million (matching the 8.97% general fund growth) to $176 million, including $5.3 million for state salary and health insurance increases and 3 new school health nurses alongside 10 unfilled positions. DPS leaders and board members (including Bettina Umstead and Matt Sears) raised concerns over the $1.1 million nurse allocation held in Public Health, regional teacher supplement competition, lifting $15/hour classified workers toward $16-$17/hour (~$4 million gap), and the need for multi-year planning and joint state Leandro advocacy, while County officials weighed tax pressures ahead of the 2022 bond.

disagreements.meeting_title: BOCC/BOE Joint Quarterly Meeting | May 10, 2022 | 9:00AM
disagreements.issue: FY23 County Funding Level for DPS ($9.88M Recommended vs. $12.875M Ask, Classified Wages, and School Nurse Funding)
disagreements.summary: DPS board members and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga pressed County leaders for greater funding beyond the County Manager's $9.88 million recommended increase to address classified wages ($16-$17/hour), teacher supplement competition, and school nurse funds, while County officials cited tax impacts and existing nurse vacancies.
disagreements.side_a_position: Increase local funding toward DPS's full ask, raise classified staff from $15/hr toward $16-$17/hr, and direct school nurse funds to address classroom/staffing needs.
side_a_arguments: DPS faces intense regional competition on teacher salary supplements and severe classified vacancies at the $15/hour wage floor (~$4M needed to reach $16-$17/hr).
Roughly $1.1 million funded previously for school health nurses stayed in County Public Health rather than coming directly to DPS.
Both boards need a multi-year funding plan and joint advocacy for state Leandro funding from the state's $6 billion rainy day fund.
disagreements.side_b_position: Hold the recommended FY23 DPS increase at $9.88 million (8.97% general fund growth) and avoid additional property tax hikes while filling existing vacancies.
side_b_arguments: The $9.88 million increase matches general fund revenue growth and covers $5.3 million in state salary/benefit pass-throughs, plus mid-year nurse funding commitment once 10 existing vacancies are filled.
Residents already face inflation at the grocery store and an upcoming 2.5-cent tax impact if the 2022 school bond passes.
State lawmakers—who refused local school board taxing authority—must fund public education rather than relying solely on local property taxes.
disagreements.resolution: Informational joint budget discussion; no formal funding vote taken at the joint meeting.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 4/21/22
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its April 21, 2022 monthly meeting, beginning with student and staff recognitions including C.E. Jordan High School's Student of the Month, Battle of the Books champion teams, and Spark Award honorees, followed by Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's report on the district's five-year accreditation review and reopening to volunteers. During general public comment and 10 online submissions, speakers urged adoption of a comprehensive district-wide gender support and inclusion policy alongside addressing racial equity, mental health, and staffing and budget shortages. Under Operations Services, staff presented planning updates for the new Durham School of the Arts recommendation—noting virtual-testing classroom needs would fall outside the current bond while keeping the existing DSA site—and reviewed the $9 million full-capacity budget and staffing challenges for Before and After School programming. The board unanimously approved the agenda, March 24 minutes, five consent agenda items, a closed session motion, and the April 21, 2022 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Celebrations: Student of the Month, Battle of the Books, and Spark Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: C.E. Jordan High School Principal Susan Taylor introduced April Student of the Month Gabriella "Gabby" Mincea, highlighting her academic excellence in math. District staff also celebrated 2022 Battle of the Books champion teams for School Library Month and presented Spark Awards to staff honorees including Ms. Parkstone, Child Nutrition Personnel Relations Supervisor Wanda McLean, and Early Childhood Instructional Coordinator Beatrice Springs.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update: Five-Year Accreditation Review and Reopening
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga reported that DPS completed its five-year district accreditation review during the prior week. He added that schools were reopening their doors to volunteers and community partners to help accelerate academic growth and recapture student learning progress.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer moved and Alexandra Valladares seconded approval of the meeting agenda as presented, which passed unanimously. Natalie Beyer then moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded approval of the March 24, 2022 monthly meeting minutes, which also passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment (In-Person and Online)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In-person commenters shared perspectives on LGBTQ+ youth, non-binary gender awareness, and urged the board to prioritize a comprehensive district-wide gender support and inclusion policy alongside racial equity, student hunger, mental health, and teacher, bus driver, and budget shortages. Staff then read 10 online public comments posted to the DPS website, including remarks from Jordan High School parent Mark Franklin supporting smooth student transitions and inclusive school environments.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval

agenda_items.title: Operations Services: New Durham School of the Arts (DSA) Recommendation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Operations staff including Frederick Davis and Dan Snitzer presented on the new Durham School of the Arts recommendation, outlining upcoming programming and planning stages with academic, operations, and community stakeholders. agenda_items.title: Before and After School Programming & Community Education Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented plans to maximize before- and after-school programming for 2022-23 while keeping tuition rates unchanged since 2015-16, offering a 10% early registration discount for the first 300 families, DSS vouchers, and 300 scholarships funded by NC Division of Child Development stabilization grants. Board members questioned waitlist dynamics, minimum enrollment thresholds, overtime pay impacts ($22.50/hr), and creative recruitment of graduating seniors and retirees ahead of May enrollment.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/24/22
meetings.executive_summary: With six board members participating (Matt Sears remotely via Zoom and Dr. Mike Lee absent), the board voted 4-2 to transition Durham Public Schools from an indoor mask mandate to mask-recommended effective April 11, 2022, after an earlier motion to make the change on April 4 failed on a 3-3 tie. Finance leadership presented the $678 million FY 2022-23 Superintendent's Proposed Budget, including a $12.875 million local funding request featuring a $4 million teacher salary supplement increase ($6,500 starting), while board members pressed to accelerate raising remaining classified wages to $17/hour ($3.7 million additional cost) and set an April 7 budget public hearing. The board also unanimously approved (5-0 after Sears dropped off Zoom) joining Durham County and the City of Durham in Duke Energy's Green Source Advantage renewable energy program, received a Cognia five-year system accreditation update, and approved the March 24 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the meeting, noting Matt Sears was participating via Zoom due to household COVID-19 positives and Dr. Mike Lee was absent. Staff recognized Riverside High School cadet Brianna Aguilar as March DPS Student of the Month, honored Burton Elementary's school social work team, and celebrated a COVID-19 Communication Award for Public Affairs and Dr. Addison-Pate.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga marked the two-year anniversary of the pandemic shift to remote learning, thanking staff for their resilience and announcing the distribution of DPS's second ESSER-funded $1,500 pre-tax retention bonus (prorated for part-time employees and substitutes working over 20 hours weekly). He also highlighted upcoming spring break, the DPS Community Fun Fair at Durham Central Park, and an upcoming job fair for certified and classified positions at Hillside High School.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval of February 24, 2022 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer moved and Alexandra Valladares seconded approval of the meeting agenda; because Matt Sears was attending remotely, the board retook the vote by roll call per counsel guidance. The board then approved the February 24, 2022 meeting minutes by roll call on a motion by Alexandra Valladares and second by Jovonia Lewis.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-0 (Roll Call for agenda and minutes)

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Seven in-person and virtual speakers addressed the board (with remaining online comments posted to the website). Six speakers (David Bomar, Ian Hembrey, Sharon Davis, Naomi Erickson Harris, Summer Sparrow, and Beth Dalton) urged ending the DPS mask mandate immediately—citing low CDC community transmission, state and municipal rollbacks, and alleged constitutional or developmental concerns—while Leslie Temple criticized math/reading proficiency levels and Natalie Spring walked in to thank the board for maintaining masks to protect students and staff.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed consent items distributed in advance and adopted the consent agenda in full without discussion or pulled items via roll call vote.

agenda_items.title: Board of Education Mask Mandate Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members debated shifting from a mask mandate to mask-recommended in light of Durham's drop to the CDC 'low' transmission level and city/county mandate lifts, while stressing readiness to reinstate masks if surges recur. Jovonia Lewis's motion (seconded by Frederick Xavier Ravin III) to move to mask-recommended on April 4 immediately after spring break failed in a 3-3 tie, after which Natalie Beyer's motion (seconded by Alexandra Valladares) to begin mask-recommended on April 11—giving nurses and staff a week post-break to prepare PPE and classroom protocols—passed 4-2.
agenda_items.vote_summary: April 4 motion failed 3-3; April 11 mask-recommended motion passed 4-2

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Proposed Budget for FY 2022-23
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur and Alex Modestou presented the $678 million FY 2022-23 proposed budget, requesting a $12.875 million local funding increase ($10.3 million for DPS plus charter pass-through) to cover $5.3 million in salary, benefit, insurance, and utility increases, $4 million to raise starting teacher salary supplements to $6,500, Lyons Farm Elementary operating costs, and seven IT technician positions phasing off ESSER. Board members discussed accelerating $17/hour classified staff wages ($3.7 million additional ask), before- and after-school care expansion, Leandro litigation updates, and holding a budget public hearing at 5:00 p.m. on April 7.

agenda_items.title: Duke Energy Green Source Advantage Program Partnership
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Monk, Fred Davis, and Director of Construction Sustainability Dan Schnitzer presented a partnership with Durham County and the City of Durham under Duke Energy's Green Source Advantage program to procure solar energy offsets through operational rather than capital funds. Board members praised the interlocal collaboration toward DPS's 80% by 2030 and 100% by 2050 renewable energy goals and asked about future battery storage and energy dashboards before approving the partnership.

agenda_items.title: Five-Year System Accreditation Update (Cognia)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Director of School Innovation Ashley Stevens outlined DPS's transition to Cognia system-wide accreditation across all 54 schools ahead of the April 11 engagement review. They highlighted five-year strategic plan progress including unanimous equity policy adoption, 1-to-1 device rollout, indoor air quality upgrades, new school construction, and stakeholder panel preparations.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session at 02:50:40 on a motion by Alexandra Valladares and second by Jovonia Lewis. Returning to open session at 03:15:07, the board unanimously approved the March 24, 2022 personnel report before adjourning.

side_a_arguments: Durham had reached the CDC 'low' transmission level and both the city and county had lifted indoor mask mandates.
Spring break already gave families a week to prepare, and the board could use its scheduled April 7 meeting to reinstate masks if metrics worsened.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay the transition to mask-recommended until Monday, April 11, 2022, one week after spring break.
side_b_arguments: Teachers, nurses, and school staff would be on spring break and needed non-break workdays to verify KN95/clear mask inventory, arrange classroom accommodations, and brief the board on April 7 on keeping classrooms open.
Waiting one week after spring break would help detect any post-travel BA.2 Omicron spikes before removing the mandate.
disagreements.resolution: The April 4 motion failed 3-3; Matt Sears then joined Natalie Beyer, Alexandra Valladares, and Bettina Umstead to approve the April 11 effective date 4-2 (with Frederick Xavier Ravin III and Jovonia Lewis voting No and Dr. Mike Lee absent).

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education | Work Session | 3/10/22
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 10, 2022 work session, the full board unanimously amended the agenda to add a mask mandate discussion and vote and ultimately voted 7-0 to adopt administration recommendations ending outdoor masking requirements and adjusting athletic event protocols effective March 16, while Frederick Xavier Ravin III withdrew a second motion to renew the indoor mask mandate early so the board could take it up with full public notice on March 24. The board received Strategic Plan Priority 3 and HR classification/compensation study updates showing teacher turnover climbing to 18.7% (projected ~20%), prompting urgent board calls to include $17/hour classified staff raises ($3.7-$4.4 million) in the FY 2022-23 budget rather than waiting until FY 2023-24. The board also approved consent items A-E, advanced people-first homelessness policy revisions (Policy 4125) to March 24 second reading, adopted the Arts in Our Schools Month proclamation, and approved the March 10 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Amendment/Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead convened the work session and led a moment of silence. Frederick Xavier Ravin III moved to amend the agenda to add a mask mandate discussion and vote at Item 9B; despite concern about surprising staff and fellow board members without advance materials, the board approved the amendment 7-0, adopted the amended agenda 7-0, and approved the February 10, 2022 work session minutes 7-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Amendment, amended agenda, and minutes each passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Two in-person speakers (Umberto Trejo and Carmen Beltran) thanked the board for maintaining safety protections and urged deeper parent inclusion, while staff read 30-second excerpts from 144 online submissions during the 30-minute window. Online commenters were sharply divided between lifting the school mask mandate to match Durham City/County and neighboring districts and keeping masks to protect immunocompromised students and staff, alongside parents urging expanded after-school care budgets ahead of the 2:15 p.m. elementary dismissal shift.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-E)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved consent items A through E reviewed earlier in committees: the 2022-23 E-Rate application, data protection backup/restore hardware purchase, Elementary School F construction materials testing and special inspections contract, building services preferred brands list, and 2022-23 specialty school calendars.

agenda_items.title: Policy Revisions: People-First Language for Students Experiencing Homelessness (Policy 4125)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff/Legal Officer Tanya Giovanni and Dr. Bullock (Office of Equity Affairs) presented roughly 100 revisions across eight board policies—led by Policy 4125—replacing 'homeless students' with 'students experiencing homelessness' and 'homeless liaison' with 'McKinney-Vento liaison.' Board members asked staff to ensure visible McKinney-Vento links on all school websites and voted 7-0 to place the policies on the March 24 consent agenda for second reading and adoption.

agenda_items.title: Arts in Our Schools Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Arts Education Director Jeremy Tucker previewed district spring concerts, art exhibitions, and the March 19 DPS Fest community fun fair at Durham Central Park. Board members read aloud and unanimously adopted the proclamation declaring March 2022 as Arts in Our Schools Month.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 3 Update: Attract and Retain Outstanding Educators and Staff
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR leaders Dr. Alvera Lassane, Kimberly Hager, and Jeff Coek reported teacher turnover rising to 18.7% (projected near 20% by year-end) alongside acute vacancies in Exceptional Children, elementary, math, science, and bus drivers, while noting a 0.2% increase in Hispanic/Latino hires and 101 international teachers. Board members pressed for urgent action on classified wages, substitute pipelines, bilingual bonuses, and affordable staff housing.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Classification and Compensation Study Process Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Alvera Lassane outlined a comprehensive RFP-based classification and compensation study (closing April 15, final report December 8, 2022) intended to inform FY 2023-24 pay adjustments with no retroactive pay. Board members warned that classified staff and instructional assistants could not wait until 2023-24, leading Superintendent Dr. Mubenga to note staff had costed raising non-bus-driver classified staff to $17/hour at $3.7-$4.4 million if added to the FY 2022-23 budget request (~$17.2 million total).

agenda_items.title: Mask Mandate Discussion and Outdoor Masking Vote (Item 9B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Frederick Xavier Ravin III initiated discussion on revisiting the mask mandate following city, county, and CDC changes, and Dr. Hardy presented administrative guidance recommending making outdoor masking and athletic spectator protocols optional. The board voted 7-0 to adopt the administration's outdoor masking and safety recommendations effective Wednesday, March 16, 2022; Ravin also moved to renew the indoor mask mandate until March 24, but withdrew the motion after board members agreed indoor masking should wait for the noticed March 24 regular meeting.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Outdoor masking recommendations passed 7-0; indoor renewal motion withdrawn

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Summary, Closed Session, and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a summary of follow-up items (with Dr. Mike Lee recognized as work-session segment chair), the board voted 7-0 to enter closed session at 02:59:16. Returning to open session at 03:13:53, the board unanimously approved the March 10, 2022 personnel report.
