disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education | Work Session | 3/10/22
disagreements.issue: Adding Unnoticed Mask Mandate Vote to Work Session and Timing of Indoor Mandate Vote
disagreements.summary: Board members debated both the procedural propriety of adding an unnoticed mask mandate vote to a work session agenda and whether to vote immediately on renewing the indoor mandate rather than waiting for the March 24 regular meeting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Add the mask mandate vote to the work session agenda and act on both outdoor recommendations and renewing the indoor mandate.
side_a_arguments: Major shifts had occurred since the February 24 vote, including Durham City and County lifting mandates and updated CDC guidance.
Renewing the indoor mandate during the March 10 session would satisfy the monthly statutory requirement for March.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid surprising staff without advance materials and defer any indoor mask mandate vote until the regularly noticed March 24 meeting.
side_b_arguments: Best governance practice is giving the superintendent, staff, fellow board members, and community advance notice and background materials before agenda votes.
Community members did not expect an indoor mask mandate decision at a work session and should have full notice ahead of March 24.
disagreements.resolution: The board approved adding Item 9B and voted 7-0 to adopt outdoor masking relaxation effective March 16, while Frederick Xavier Ravin III withdrew his motion to renew the indoor mandate so it would be taken up on March 24.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education | Work Session | 3/10/22
disagreements.issue: Timeline for Classified Staff Pay Adjustments ($17/hr Now vs. December 2022 Compensation Study)
disagreements.summary: Administration proposed waiting for a comprehensive classification and compensation study finishing in December 2022 for FY 2023-24 implementation, whereas board members argued classified employees needed immediate FY 2022-23 wage action.
disagreements.side_a_position: Accelerate raising remaining classified staff to $17/hour in the FY 2022-23 budget request rather than waiting for the 2023-24 cycle.
side_a_arguments: Raising bus drivers to $17/hour left instructional assistants and other classified staff behind despite severe inflation and labor market competition.
Durham County added $20 million to its fund balance and instructional assistants would not wait until December 2022 or 2023-24 without retroactive pay.
disagreements.side_b_position: Use the RFP compensation study through December 2022 to build a comprehensive, sustainable pay structure for FY 2023-24 while prioritizing across-the-board teacher supplements in FY 2022-23.
side_b_arguments: A thorough internal and external vendor comparison across certified, classified, and central office roles takes until December 2022 and avoids piecemeal fixes.
Adding immediate $17/hour classified increases would expand the FY 2022-23 local budget request from ~$12.8 million to ~$17.2 million.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Superintendent Dr. Mubenga confirmed finance staff already had the $3.7-$4.4 million cost ready to include in the FY 2022-23 budget proposal if directed by the board.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | Board of Education | Monthly Meeting | 2/24/22
meetings.executive_summary: The board unanimously adopted a three-tier bell schedule alignment (7:45 a.m. elementary, 8:30 a.m. middle, 9:15 a.m. high school) for 2022-23 to stabilize bus service amid a severe driver shortage, while directing staff to expand before- and after-school care capacity. Members also voted 7-0 to continue the district's COVID-19 mask mandate after receiving 191 online public comments and mixed in-person testimony, and voted 5-2 to add Elementary School F naming to the agenda for discussion only—debating Pauli Murray versus Betty Doretha Massenberg before deferring action to March or April. Finance staff previewed a preliminary $12.8-$12.9 million FY 2022-23 local budget increase request (plus an optional $3.7 million for $17/hour classified pay), and Academic Services presented Strategic Plan Priority 1, ESL, and Exceptional Children updates before the board approved the February 24 personnel report 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the meeting with a moment of silence for the people of Ukraine following the Russian invasion. Communications Director Chip Suddeth led Student of the Month recognitions and Employee Sparkle Awards.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga reaffirmed DPS's commitment to COVID-19 safety and urged community members to get vaccinated and boosted. Dr. Nakia Hardy and Chip Suddeth presented on DPS Celebrates Black History Month programming, including a CROWN Act panel and expanded joint Black History and Women's History Month events in March.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval of Previous Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 7-0 to add a Community Safety and Wellness Task Force update (moved by Matt Sears, seconded by Natalie Beyer) and voted 5-2 to add Elementary School F naming for discussion only (moved by Frederick Xavier Ravin III, seconded by Jovonia Lewis) following objections to unscheduled additions without advance notice. The board then unanimously approved the amended agenda and prior meeting minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Task force add-on 7-0; School F discussion add-on 5-2; Amended agenda & minutes 7-0

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In-person speakers (Dana Carpenter, Jessica Schaeffer, Jenny Calderon, Millicent Rogers, Kayla Deccanto, Neil Spinner, and Matt Aeney) urged across-the-board raises and $17/hour starting pay for instructional assistants and classified staff, relief from classroom and EC staffing shortages, and lifting the mask mandate and potential student vaccine mandates. Chip Suddeth summarized 191 online comments, noting a significant majority favored continuing the mask mandate alongside comments on teacher demands and bell schedules.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-F)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following brief legal clarification from the board attorney regarding anonymous online public comments, the board unanimously adopted consent agenda items A through F on a motion by Alexandra Valladares and second by Natalie Beyer.

agenda_items.title: Board of Education Mask Mandate Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Dr. Mike Lee and second by Natalie Beyer, the board voted unanimously without additional debate to continue the DPS mask mandate.

agenda_items.title: Community Wellness and Safety Task Force Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis reported that educator representative Tanya Leathers had stepped down for personal reasons and proposed an application window from February 28 to March 28, with the board voting on a replacement at its April 7 work session.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Naming Elementary School F
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Frederick Xavier Ravin III advocated naming Elementary School F after Betty Doretha Massenberg, Durham's first Black female city school principal, while Chip Suddeth recounted that Pauli Murray had been the top recommendation in the October 21 survey before substantial community support emerged for Massenberg. Alexandra Valladares expressed support for Massenberg or Murray-Massenberg, and Jovonia Lewis questioned repeated deferrals since October; Chair Umstead noted the item was added for discussion only and would return for action in March or April.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Deferred to March or April

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: DPS Bell Schedule Alignment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Monk, Matthew Palmer, and Joe Harris presented a plan to align all schools into a true three-tier bell schedule in 2022-23 (7:45 a.m. elementary, 8:30 a.m. middle, 9:15 a.m. high) to manage 429 routes with a rolling daily average of 120 bus drivers, cut ride times, and reach the 95.8% state efficiency target. Board members voted 7-0 to adopt the alignment while directing administration to return with a robust plan eliminating before- and after-school care waitlists.

agenda_items.title: 2022-23 Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Paul LeSieur and Alex Modestou detailed the preliminary $12.8-$12.9 million FY 2022-23 local funding increase ($10.3 million DPS + $2.5 million charter pass-through), $600,000 in internal reallocations (including $350,000 for coaching stipends and $90,000 for Office of Equity Affairs), and an estimated $3.7 million additional cost to raise classified starting wages to $17/hour. Board members urged prioritizing $17/hour classified pay, higher substitute pay, mental health counselors and social workers, and affordable staff housing.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Strategic Plan Priority 1, ESL, and Exceptional Children Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and academic staff reviewed Strategic Plan Priority 1 metrics (graduation rate rising to 87%, teacher technology utilization at 79%, and 54% grade-level proficiency against a 60% goal), a new Elna B. Spaulding Conflict Resolution Center truancy partnership, and Exceptional Children and ESL updates. Board members emphasized targeted summer supports for second graders and highlighted how county funding gaps correlate with performance trends.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board amended its closed session motion to add a confidential student matter under GS 143-318.11(a)(6) and GS 115C-402 and entered closed session 7-0. Returning to open session at 05:35:31, the board unanimously approved the February 24, 2022 personnel report.

votes.discussion_detail: Matt Sears moved and Natalie Beyer seconded adding Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis's Community Safety and Wellness Task Force update to the agenda; passed unanimously.

votes.notes: Voice vote; mover Ravin and seconder Lewis supported, while individual votes of the five ayes and two nays were not called or named on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: Frederick Xavier Ravin III moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded adding Elementary School F naming to the agenda; after clarification that the addition was for discussion only (not action) and concern over unreadiness without prior notice, the motion passed 5-2.

votes.item_title: Approve February 24, 2022 Meeting Agenda as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded approval of the full agenda as amended with Items 9B and 9C; passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Approve Previous Board of Education Monthly Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded approval of the prior monthly meeting minutes as presented; passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Continue DPS COVID-19 Mask Mandate
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded continuing the DPS mask mandate; passed 7-0 without further discussion.

votes.item_title: Adopt 2022-23 Three-Tier Bell Schedule Alignment (7:45 a.m. / 8:30 a.m. / 9:15 a.m.)
votes.discussion_detail: Following extensive discussion of bus route efficiency, special needs ride times, and expanded after-school care needs, Matt Sears moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded adopting the three-tier bell schedule alignment for 2022-23, passing unanimously.

votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded entering closed session with an amendment adding a confidential student matter under GS 143-318.11(a)(6) and GS 115C-402; passed unanimously.

votes.discussion_detail: Upon returning to open session at 05:35:31, Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the February 24, 2022 personnel report; passed unanimously.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | Board of Education | Monthly Meeting | 2/24/22
disagreements.issue: Scheduling Action and Name Selection for Elementary School F (Pauli Murray vs. Betty Doretha Massenberg)
disagreements.summary: Board members split 5-2 over adding Elementary School F naming to the February 24 agenda without prior notice, and disagreed over whether to proceed immediately to a vote or defer action to a future meeting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Bring Elementary School F naming back immediately for board discussion and potential decision, favoring Betty Doretha Massenberg (or Murray-Massenberg).
side_a_arguments: The naming item had already appeared on October 21, November 18, and December 9 agendas, and community due diligence and public advocacy for Betty Doretha Massenberg were complete.
Deferring repeatedly without explanation left the community waiting to give the new school its identity.
disagreements.side_b_position: Restrict the unscheduled agenda addition to discussion only and defer any final vote to a noticed March or April meeting.

Because the item was added only for discussion, taking action without amending the agenda again would be procedurally improper.
disagreements.resolution: The board voted 5-2 to add the item for discussion only, heard remarks from Ravin, Valladares, Lewis, and Chip Suddeth, and deferred a formal vote to a March or April agenda.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOE/BOCC Quarterly Meeting February 15, 2022 9:00 AM
meetings.executive_summary: At the quarterly joint meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners and DPS Board of Education—co-chaired by BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and DPS Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis with five DPS members present (Bettina Umstead and Dr. Mike Lee absent at a conference)—the two boards unanimously approved the November 16, 2021 joint minutes. County management committed to recommending full funding in the Capital Improvement Plan and upcoming 2022 General Obligation bond referendum for DPS's increased school construction and renovation scope (Elementary School F, new Northern and Jordan high schools, and DSA, Glenn, and E.K. Powe renovations), alongside a joint MWBE disparity study and renewable energy collaboration. DPS CFO Paul LeSieur also presented ESSER I-III spending (including three $1,500 retention bonuses) and previewed a $12.8 million preliminary FY 2022-23 local budget request plus $3.7 million if all classified pay is raised to $17/hour, while county staff presented their FY 2022-23 budget outlook.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Review, and Approval of November 16, 2021 Joint Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and DPS Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis co-chaired the virtual joint meeting with BOCC Commissioners Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Nimasheena Burns (joined later) and DPS Board Members Jovonia Lewis, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Natalie Beyer, Matt Sears, and Alexandra Valladares (Chairs Brenda Howerton and Bettina Umstead, and Dr. Mike Lee, absent). Moved by Commissioner Carter and seconded by Natalie Beyer, the November 16, 2021 joint minutes passed unanimously by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) and General Obligation (GO) Bond Referendum Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and County Budget Director Keith Lane outlined the CIP schedule (March adoption, April bond market testing, June 14 preliminary GO bond resolution) and stated county management would recommend fully funding DPS's cost increases driven by scope changes, pre-K class-size legislation, and construction inflation. Officials also highlighted solar-ready roofing and renewable energy bulk-buying opportunities following the BOCC's renewable energy plan adoption, plus a joint Durham County-DPS disparity study.

agenda_items.title: DPS Federal COVID Relief (ESSER) and FY 2022-23 Local Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS CFO Paul LeSieur reviewed $155 million in ESSER II/III allocations (including $34.4 million for HVAC/facilities, $25 million for summer learning, 23 mental health/school counselors, and $1,500 retention bonuses in November 2021, March 2022, and October 2022) and presented DPS's preliminary $12.8 million FY 2022-23 local request ($10.3 million DPS + $2.5 million charter pass-through) covering a $4 million teacher supplement increase to $6,500 starting, $17/hour bus driver pay, Lyons Farm staffing, and 7 IT technicians. Commissioners and board members discussed moving all classified workers toward $17/hour ($3.7 million additional cost), staff mental health, and whether federal ARPA/ESSER final rules barred aggregate affordable teacher housing.

agenda_items.title: Durham County FY 2022-23 Budget Process Update and Closing Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane reviewed county revenue projections, rising employee health insurance ($4.5-$5 million) and state retirement costs, departmental SWOT analyses, and key budget dates (May 9 manager recommendation, June 13 adoption). Joint members closed by emphasizing mental health investments, living wages, staffing retention, and scheduling a Durham Pre-K update for the next joint meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 16, 2021 Joint BOE/BOCC Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: DPS Chair Bettina Umstead and Board Member Dr. Mike Lee were absent. BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs co-chaired with DPS Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis; BOCC Commissioners Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Wendy Jacobs also voted Aye.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education | Work Session | 2/10/22
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its February 10, 2022 work session, starting with 5-0 approvals of the agenda and January 13 minutes before unanimously approving the six-item consent agenda and a proclamation designating February 2022 as Career and Technical Education (CTE) Month. Online public commenters raised concerns over COVID-19 masking and staff vaccination rates, late-night closure communications, and a request to use federal ESSER funds for $5,000 employee retention bonuses. Staff presented Strategic Plan Priority 2 updates showing reductions in restorative practice center referrals and short-term suspensions across more than half of DPS schools, alongside Panorama social-emotional learning data, COVID-19 employee vaccination tracking, and the Durham Safe Routes to School partnership with Bike Durham. In its major financial action, the board unanimously approved reallocating federal ESSER funds for staff bonuses—complementing local classified bonuses and county teacher supplement requests—and closed the meeting by unanimously approving the February 10 personnel report after a brief closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the work session to order, acknowledged the Spanish interpreters, and led a moment of silence. The board approved the agenda (moved by Dr. Mike Lee, seconded by Natalie Beyer) and the January 13, 2022 work session minutes (moved by Natalie Beyer, seconded by Dr. Mike Lee), with both measures passing 5-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment (Online)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no in-person speakers signed up, staff read three online public comments. One commenter questioned mask enforcement, student behavior, and unvaccinated staff; an anonymous working parent criticized late-night school closure calls; and parent Sarah Miller urged the board to use federal ESSER funds for $5,000 staff retention bonuses and added monthly teacher planning time.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items A-F)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Umstead presented the six-item consent agenda (Items A through F), noting board and staff had reviewed the items in detail prior to the meeting. Natalie Beyer moved and Bettina Umstead seconded approval of all consent items, passing unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: 2022 Career and Technical Education (CTE) Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Academic Services staff thanked the board for supporting CTE and the 3-2-1 work-based learning initiative and presented a proclamation designating February 2022 as CTE Month in Durham Public Schools. Bettina Umstead moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded adoption of the proclamation, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services Item 7D: Strategic Plan Priority 2 Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Spencer presented the 2021-22 Strategic Plan Priority 2 update, highlighting stakeholder feedback loops and discipline data showing decreases in restorative practice center referrals and short-term suspensions at more than half of DPS schools. Staff also reviewed Panorama student social-emotional learning (SEL) survey domains, SPARCS trauma-support groups, newly added school-based mental health counselors, and restorative practice center learning walks.

agenda_items.title: Reallocation of Federal ESSER Funds for Staff Bonuses and Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff reviewed state versus local staffing ratios, adjustments reducing capital/operations allocations from $65 million to $55 million and recouping unspent summer learning funds to assemble $15 million, prior classified bonuses, local teacher supplement increases (seeking $4 million from the county to raise starting supplements to $6,500), and DPS's ASBO and GFOA Awards of Excellence. Natalie Beyer moved and Bettina Umstead seconded approving the reallocation of federal ESSER funds for staff bonuses; Chair Umstead praised staff responsiveness to an educator bonus petition ahead of upcoming meetings with Durham County Commissioners, and the motion passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Operations Services Item 8B: COVID-19 Vaccination Mandate and Testing Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated the board on elementary and district-wide employee COVID-19 vaccination statuses, follow-up for unvaccinated staff working near students, state versus local leave policies, and student vaccination attestation forms that avoid five-day exposure quarantines. Chair Umstead and Natalie Beyer requested greater promotion of student attestation forms and a future presentation on lessons learned from the student-athlete and extracurricular vaccination/testing mandate.

agenda_items.title: Operations Services Item 8C: Durham Safe Routes to School Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Operations staff and Bike Durham partners presented the Durham Safe Routes to School program, aimed at easing school drop-off/pick-up traffic congestion and expanding May Bike to School Day participation toward a goal of 20 schools. Board members discussed coordinating community bike donations through the DPS Foundation and leveraging active transportation for after-school programming, before summarizing requested follow-ups on driver's education staffing and athletics vaccination data.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Approval of February 10, 2022 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Prior to seconding the closed-session motion, a board member announced the Equity Affairs Department's February 28 CROWN Act event at Hillside High School kicking off CROWN Act Week (March 1-7). Alexandra Valladares moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded entering closed session, passing by voice vote; upon returning to open session at 02:54:49, Jovonia Lewis moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approving the February 10, 2022 personnel report, which passed unanimously before adjournment.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously; Personnel report passed unanimously

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | Board of Education | Monthly Meeting | 1/27/22
meetings.executive_summary: In a unanimous monthly meeting, the board voted 7-0 to continue the DPS COVID-19 mask mandate, adopted both the 2022-23 and 2023-24 traditional and year-round school calendars with aligned spring breaks, and approved a proclamation declaring January 2022 as National Mentoring Month. Public commenters—especially instructional assistants—pressed for $19-$22/hour across-the-board pay raises and uniform overtime and break policies, while speakers also addressed mentoring and COVID-19 mitigation. The board received presentations on the countywide 'Grown in Durham' Early Childhood Action Plan and DPS's 25% aspirational MWBE procurement goal, approved consent contracts for DSA and Lyons Farm Elementary, and approved the January 27 personnel report 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the meeting (noting temporary DPSNC.net networking issues), led a moment of silence, and joined Northern High School Principal Danny Gilford in honoring Student of the Month Jameleth, followed by special recognition for educators Turquoise LeJune Parker and Greg DeSette.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga highlighted COVID-19 contact tracing, testing, and vaccination town halls co-hosted with the Old North State Medical Society through February, and previewed upcoming community engagement around DPS's new student assignment policy and Growing Together regions.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jovonia Lewis moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the January 27, 2022 agenda as presented, passing unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Instructional assistants and advocates including Andre Robinson and Edwin Carter-Kerr urged raising starting IA pay to $19-$22/hour across all experience steps and establishing a district-wide IA policy on overtime, breaks, and class coverage. Community pediatrician Walker Robinson, mentoring advocate DeWarren Langley, and other speakers addressed student health, mentoring, and COVID-19 masking.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved two consent items on a motion by Dr. Mike Lee and second by Natalie Beyer: a Durham School of the Arts fan coil replacement contract with Comfort Mechanical Contractors and a Lyons Farm Elementary soil stabilization change order.

agenda_items.title: Board of Education Mask Mandate Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a motion to continue the DPS mask mandate, Natalie Beyer shared personal remarks about her father's COVID-19 illness and urged relying on public health science and vaccinations. The board voted 7-0 to maintain the mask mandate.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for National Mentoring Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the request of community member DeWarren Langley, board members took turns reading aloud and unanimously adopted a proclamation declaring January 2022 as National Mentoring Month and supporting critical mentoring for youth and boys of color.

agenda_items.title: Early Childhood Action Plan ('Grown in Durham')
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis, Durham Children's Initiative President David Reese, Durham County Early Childhood Coordinator Kate Elander, ECAP Manager Bonnie DeLan, and parent leader Umberto Trejo presented the 21-recommendation birth-to-age-8 action plan built with 50+ organizations and 1,500+ residents. Discussion centered on DPS's partnership across Pre-K expansion, trauma-informed classrooms, language justice, developmental inclusion, transportation barriers, and leveraging county ARPA funding.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Two-Year Instructional Calendar Adoption (2022-23 and 2023-24)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Ashley Stevens presented two-year traditional and year-round instructional calendars aligned around spring break intercessions and expanded holiday inclusivity. After questions on inclement-weather virtual learning, election-day adjustments, and community vote margins on 2023-24 spring break timing, the board voted 7-0 to adopt the calendars.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Minority and Women Business Enterprises (MWBE) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Monk and Farad Ali of the National Economic Development Institute updated the board on DPS's MWBE outreach and 25% aspirational procurement goal across construction and maintenance projects. Board members praised county collaboration and Frederick Xavier Ravin III asked whether livable-wage clauses could be explored in vendor contracts.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 7-0 to enter closed session on a motion by Dr. Mike Lee and second by Natalie Beyer. Returning to open session at 03:12:13, the board unanimously approved the January 27, 2022 personnel report.

votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer moved and Alexandra Valladares seconded adopting the 2022-23 and 2023-24 traditional and year-round school calendars as presented by administration; passed unanimously.

meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Work Session Chair Natalie Beyer, the board unanimously approved its amended agenda, December 9, 2021 minutes, consent items (secondary math curriculum adoption and revised 2021-22 school calendars), and the FY 2020-21 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report showing clean unmodified audit opinions and a $16.59 million local current expense fund balance. Finance staff opened the FY 2022-23 budget cycle by outlining a preliminary $12.9 million local funding increase ($10.3 million DPS plus charter pass-through) featuring a $4 million teacher salary supplement boost, while flagging an extra ~$4 million cost to raise all classified wages to $17/hour. agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda/Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Chair Natalie Beyer convened the work session and led a moment of silence. The board amended closed session to add a student transfer appeal, approved the amended agenda 7-0 (moved by Bettina Umstead, seconded by Dr. Mike Lee), and approved the December 9, 2021 work session minutes 7-0 (moved by Dr. Mike Lee, seconded by Jovonia Lewis).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Amended agenda and minutes each passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Riverside High School parent Jenny Martinez spoke in person with interpretation regarding an incident with a school official and alleged discrimination. agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda

agenda_items.vote_summary: Accepted without objection / No vote required

agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur and auditor Paul Carson (Anderson Smith & Wike PLLC) presented the FY 2020-21 audit, issuing clean unmodified opinions on financial statements and federal/state compliance with zero material weaknesses or grant repayment findings, a $16,587,039 local current expense fund balance, $6.2 million capital outlay fund balance, and $1.2 million food service net profit. Board members approved the audit 7-0 on a motion by Bettina Umstead and second by Frederick Xavier Ravin III.

agenda_items.title: FY 2022-23 Budget Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Paul LeSieur and Alex Modestou introduced the FY 2022-23 budget cycle, projecting a $12.9 million local funding increase ($10.3 million DPS + ~$2.6 million charter pass-through at ~20% charter share) for 2.5% raises, bus driver pay ($17-$24/hour), health/retirement inflation, a $4 million teacher supplement increase ($6,500 starting), Lyons Farm operations, and 7 IT technicians. Board members discussed an additional ~$4 million to raise all classified wages to $17/hour without salary compression, ESOL/EC funding caps, and federal ESSER reporting transparency.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services & HR: COVID-19 Response, Testing, and Employee Vaccine Mandate Update

Board members raised concerns over contagious disease leave documentation burdens, pandemic EBT absence coding (Code 1D), and state laws restricting remote shifts during the Omicron surge.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education | Work Session | 12/9/21
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its December 9, 2021 work session (presided over by Work Session Chair Frederick Xavier Ravin III, with Board Chair Bettina Umstead presiding after closed session), pulling the naming of Elementary School F to January and unanimously approving the revised 2021-22 calendar, Policy 4150 (School Assignment) on second reading, Ignite Online Academy equipment, and continuing the district mask mandate. Operational Services staff presented updated Lyons Farm Elementary attendance boundaries to relieve severe overcrowding at Creekside Elementary; despite member concerns over denying district bus transportation to roughly 30 grandfathered students remaining at Parkwood, the board passed the boundaries unanimously. The board also held an extended discussion on staff COVID-19 vaccination mandate compliance, with members pushing administration on why roughly 1,400 unvaccinated staff were effectively operating under a weekly testing regime and requesting vaccine incentives, nurse visits to maintenance and transportation hubs, and potential recovery sick-day credits. Following a closed session, the board unanimously approved the December 9, 2021 personnel report before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Student of the Month, and COVID-19 Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The work session opened with a welcome, recognition of interpreters Martha Romo Aguiles and Marty Ramirez, and a moment of silence. While waiting for the delayed Student of the Month (later celebrated at 00:09:15-00:14:02), Dr. Pascal Mubenga addressed recent COVID-19 emails and subsequently clarified student vaccination rates at 29.38% for ages 5-11 and 50% for ages 12-18.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: It was noted that the naming of Elementary School F had been pulled from the agenda and moved to January for additional consideration. The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the agenda as presented by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 4, 2021 Board Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the November 4, 2021 work session minutes. A motion and second were made and the minutes passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board heard one in-person speaker (Melissa Rogers) and two online comments (including Paige McCullough reading on behalf of Vanessa Barnett-Loro of E.K. Powe). Remarks covered potentially naming a future school after Frederick Xavier Ravin III, establishing outdoor lunch across all DPS schools rather than leaving it to individual principals, and reporting COVID-19 statistics regularly at meetings and online.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Mask Mandate Continuation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The consent agenda comprised five items: a revised 2021-22 calendar, Policy 4150 (School Assignment) second reading, an Ignite Online Academy equipment purchase from Progressive Business Solutions, approval to negotiate professional program/project management services, and a Lakeview School rooftop unit replacement contract with Comfort Mechanical. Following unanimous consent approval and a request to communicate Policy 4150 updates clearly to families, the board unanimously voted to continue the DPS mask mandate.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consent agenda passed 7-0; Mask mandate continuation passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Lyons Farm Elementary Attendance Boundary
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk and Matthew Palmer presented updated attendance boundary recommendations for Lyons Farm Elementary to relieve severe overcrowding at Creekside Elementary while balancing socioeconomic diversity. Students in grades 2-4 who were previously shifted from Creekside to Parkwood in 2019 would have the option to stay at Parkwood without district busing or move to Lyons Farm; a board member questioned withholding transportation as an equity barrier for non-car-rider families before the board approved the recommendation unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Staff COVID-19 Vaccination Mandate Implementation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated the board on progress toward the 100% staff vaccination mandate goal, noting staff positive cases fell from 60+ per month prior to the mandate to roughly 20 per month (134 total, or 2% of 5,400+ employees in 2021-22). Matt Sears and other members expressed concern that allowing weekly testing for ~1,400 unvaccinated staff meant DPS was functioning like a testing mandate rather than a vaccine mandate, and urged mobile nurse vaccine visits to maintenance and transportation centers, single-dose follow-up data, Spanish flyers, ESSER-funded support staff, and paid recovery time for shot side effects.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized three follow-up items: providing a family-friendly summary of Policy 4150, coordinating with the Durham County Health Department on vaccine allotments and on-site education/administration, and returning in January with employee vaccination incentive options. meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOE/BOCC Quarterly Meeting November 16, 2021 9:00 AM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham Board of County Commissioners held their November 16, 2021 quarterly joint meeting, unanimously approving the August 17, 2021 joint minutes via roll call before reviewing escalating 10-year Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) projections. County budget officials presented the combined five-year CIP request surging from $400 million to over $1 billion—calling it a 'tidal wave' driven by construction inflation, supply chain delays, and expanded DPS and county project scopes—which prompted pushback from Dr. Mike Lee against portraying DPS capital requests as excessive or mismanaged rather than overdue responses to deferred maintenance and state underfunding. Both boards also discussed factoring solar-ready and renewable energy costs into upcoming school construction, expanding capacity at a replacement Durham School of the Arts beyond 1,500 seats, and exploring joint disparity studies. After a brief five-minute Pre-K overview deferred for full discussion to February 2022, both boards approved the 2022 joint meeting schedule by roll call.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the joint BOE/BOCC meeting to order with no agenda adjustments. agenda_items.discussion_summary: County officials presented a 'tidal wave' chart showing five-year total CIP requests growing from $400M (2020-24) to over $1B (2022-26), including DPS five-year projects rising from $110M to $352M and non-DPS county projects reaching $418M over five years ($719M over 10 years), citing labor shortages, inflation, LGC scrutiny, and state K-12 deferred maintenance. Dr. Mike Lee pushed back on the framing to counter public narratives of DPS fiscal mismanagement, emphasizing that capital needs grow exponentially when deferred. Boards also discussed incorporating solar/renewable energy costs, increasing Durham School of the Arts capacity above 1,500 (to address 1,800-1,900 enrollment), debt/tax modeling, and joint disparity studies with Dr. Julius Monk.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The boards considered the proposed 2022 joint meeting schedule beginning in February 2022. Natalie Beyer moved, seconded by Alexandra Valladares and Commissioner Nida Allam, and the schedule was approved by joint roll call vote before adjournment.

disagreements.issue: Framing of Escalating DPS Capital Improvement Plan Costs ('Tidal Wave' vs. Deferred Needs)
disagreements.summary: County budget officials framed the jump in five-year CIP requests from $400M to over $1B as an unaffordable 'tidal wave' requiring scrutiny of shovel-readiness and LGC/rating-agency capacity, while Dr. Mike Lee objected to rhetoric implying DPS was inflating requests rather than addressing overdue deferred maintenance and construction inflation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Highlight the rapid expansion of CIP spending requests as a fiscal 'tidal wave' exceeding historical spend patterns and potentially beyond county affordability without strict prioritization.
side_a_arguments: Five-year CIP requests climbed from $400M two years ago to over $1B, with DPS's 5-year request jumping from $110M to $352M.
The Local Government Commission (LGC) and bond rating agencies will scrutinize debt authorizations compared to historical spend capacity.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject narratives suggesting DPS is padding or mismanaging its capital budget, emphasizing that cost growth stems from inflation, state underfunding, and compounding deferred facility needs.
side_b_arguments: Deferring school repairs causes nonlinear, exponential future cost increases ('future cost of money').
The DPS facility master plan reflects genuine, professionally vetted district survival needs rather than 'pork' or discretionary add-ons.
disagreements.resolution: County Manager Claudia Hager clarified the chart also reflected K-12 state underfunding and county project growth ($719M non-DPS), and both boards committed to reviewing debt-capacity and tax scenarios together ahead of February 2022.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Public Hearing October 21, 2021 5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education convened a public hearing on October 21, 2021 to review proposed school board election district maps (Options B, C, D, and E) ahead of its November 4 vote. Demographer Blake Esselstyn and legal counsel Ms. Wagner presented population deviation, compactness, and racial demographic comparisons across the consultant-drawn options and Option E—submitted by Board Member Frederick Xavier Ravin III—noting that Option E prioritized accommodating future growth over compactness and dispersed Black/African American populations somewhat in consolidated districts. Chair Bettina Umstead declined Ravin's request to advocate for Option E during the hearing so the session remained centered on expert analysis and public feedback. Submitted online comments split sharply, with supporters praising Option E's attention to East Durham growth and communities of interest, while opponents urged rejecting Option E as an improper, non-transparent map drawn by a sitting board member.

agenda_items.title: Redistricting Presentation and Legal/Demographic Analysis (Options B, C, D, and E)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Demographer Blake Esselstyn walked through Durham County population growth patterns and compared Options B, C, D, and member-submitted Option E. Legal counsel Ms. Wagner and Esselstyn addressed board questions on compactness, north-south vs. side-by-side district configurations, and racial balance across consolidated Districts A and B and Districts 3 and 4; Chair Umstead declined Frederick Xavier Ravin III's request to explain Option E further during the hearing to keep the focus on expert presentation and public comment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Comments on Redistricting Maps
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no in-person speakers present, Mr. Sutter read online public comments submitted for the hearing. Speakers including Kenya Dumas supported Option C (or D), Vicki Miller, Gina Chung, and Antonio Jones backed Option E for anticipating East Durham growth and keeping Districts 1 and 2 together, while Rachel Holtzman, an anonymous teacher, Paige McCullough, Rann Bar-On, and Sarah Anderson urged rejecting Option E as inappropriate self-drawing by a sitting board member; Chair Umstead closed the hearing and stated the board would vote at its November 4 work session.

disagreements.summary: Public commenters and board members clashed over the legitimacy and merits of Option E, drawn by sitting Board Member Frederick Xavier Ravin III outside the independent consultant process, versus consultant-crafted Options B, C, and D.
disagreements.side_a_position: Include and consider Option E because it uses data trends to accommodate future East Durham population growth and keeps Districts 1 and 2 together as communities of interest.

disagreements.side_b_position: Reject Option E and choose exclusively from maps drawn by independent, neutral consultants to protect process integrity and compactness.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting September 23, 2021 6:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Spark Scholars Virtual Program Magnet-Seat Retention and Edmentum Contract Approval
disagreements.summary: Board members debated whether students transferring from magnet schools into the one-year Spark Scholars virtual stopgap program should keep their magnet seats for the following year, and whether to separate the Edmentum contract vote from that programmatic rule. The contract passed 6-1 by voice vote.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the up-to-$825,000 Edmentum contract directly so Spark Scholars can launch promptly without delaying on magnet-seat rules, while honoring Ignite's advance commitment process.
side_a_arguments: Edmentum provides immediate virtual staffing stability for up to 300 waitlisted students given current teacher shortages.
Ignite Online Academy is the permanent pathway where families committed during the application window, whereas Spark Scholars is a one-year stopgap.
disagreements.side_b_position: Allow Spark Scholars families from magnet schools to retain their magnet seats without penalty—or address the programmatic rule alongside the contract—rather than forcing them back into the lottery.
side_b_arguments: Because Spark Scholars is explicitly a one-year temporary program during the Delta surge for medically fragile or immunocompromised families, magnet schools do not lose seats this year.
Letting the handful of families return to their magnet school community without penalty is fairer than requiring re-entry into the lottery.
disagreements.resolution: Dr. Mike Lee's standalone motion to approve the up-to-$825,000 Edmentum contract passed 6-1 by voice vote (with the lone dissenter and non-moving Aye voters not named in the voice vote).

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education convened its September 9, 2021 work session (presided over by Work Session Chair Frederick Xavier Ravin III, with Chair Bettina Umstead presiding after closed session), adding a general COVID-19 update to the agenda and hearing 46 submitted public comments—dominated by urgent appeals to mandate outdoor eating district-wide, improve bus driver pay and staffing, and adopt a staff vaccine mandate—plus two in-person speakers. disagreements.summary: Ahead of passing the staff vaccine mandate, board members differed on whether unvaccinated employees without medical or religious exemptions should be permitted weekly testing as an alternative or face stricter consequences.
disagreements.side_a_position: Allow administrative discretion to require weekly testing for employees who decline vaccination.
side_a_arguments: Weekly testing provides a practical safeguard while accommodating administrative discretion on non-vaccinated staff.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject testing as a general opt-out and limit testing accommodations strictly to approved religious or medical exemptions.
side_b_arguments: The mandate should send a clear, strong statement requiring full vaccination across all ~5,200 staff rather than functioning as a testing opt-out.
Exemption procedures should cover medical and religious exemptions, while administration returns with recommendations for outright refusals.
disagreements.resolution: The board unanimously approved Attorney Ken Soo's motion mandating full vaccination by October 31, 2021 and directing administration to return with implementation details on exemptions, appeals, and exempt-staff regular testing.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Special Meeting August 31, 2021 5:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held a specially called meeting on August 31, 2021 to receive expert COVID-19 public health guidance from ABC Science Collaborative physicians. After initially voting by roll call to add a proposed bus driver pay scale increase to the agenda, Chair Bettina Umstead and Board Attorney Ken Soo determined that open-meetings notice rules for a special meeting barred acting on items outside the published call, deferring the bus driver raise to the September work session while assuring drivers the board intended to make it retroactive to August 31. ABC Collaborative doctors briefed the board on Delta variant surges, low in-school secondary transmission with universal masking, vaccine effectiveness against severe disease, 10-day isolation standards, ventilation, outdoor eating, and pediatric vaccine trial timelines for ages 5-11. Attorney Soo also clarified that expired state legislative authority precluded a district-wide shift to virtual instruction, and Frederick Xavier Ravin III formally requested administration prepare a staff vaccination incentive plan for the next meeting.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the special meeting to order (with Frederick Xavier Ravin III joining virtually and interpreters Martha Romo Aguiles and Marci Ramirez assisting) and led a moment of silence. agenda_items.discussion_summary: Duke/UNC ABC Science Collaborative doctors reviewed data showing high community transmission but low in-school secondary spread when universal masking, outdoor lunch, and proper indoor air intake/filtration are maintained, alongside 93-100% vaccine protection against hospitalization and death even with Delta. Board members questioned the experts on a recent California CDC classroom outbreak report, 10-day isolation guidelines, impracticality of daily universal testing, demographic representativeness in surveillance testing, and timelines for ages 5-11 vaccine approval (expected late October through mid-December).

meetings.title: Joint Board of Education/Board of County Commissioners Quarterly Meeting August 17, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham Board of County Commissioners held their quarterly joint meeting remotely, hosted by the County Commissioners and chaired by BOCC Chair Brenda Howerton alongside DPS Chair Bettina Umstead. Following unanimous roll-call approval of the April 18, 2021 joint meeting minutes, DPS staff and Durham PreK partners presented an early learning update detailing expansion from 61 to 65 Pre-K classrooms (858 seats) in 2021-22 and 68 classrooms (914 seats) in 2022-23 with Lyons Farm Elementary, alongside equity, Child Find, and wraparound care barriers. DPS CFO Paul LeSieur reviewed the district's $169 million county allocation (including over $11 million in new funding for operations, $6 million in capital outlay, and $250 teacher supplement increases) alongside uncertain state General Assembly budget proposals and rising retirement, health insurance, hotspot, and Pre-K costs. Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane then outlined the FY22-31 Capital Improvement Plan refresh and the timeline toward a November 8, 2022 General Obligation bond referendum amid 20-80% construction cost inflation and labor shortages, before Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga requested Sheriff/City traffic assistance and 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. community COVID testing sites for school reopening.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Approval of April 18, 2021 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Clerk Monica Toomer confirmed a quorum of County Commissioners and DPS Board of Education members online, and BOCC Chair Brenda Howerton called the meeting to order at 9:00 a.m. with no agenda adjustments. After confirming two name corrections requested by BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs were included in the packet, the joint boards approved the April 18, 2021 minutes by roll call vote.

agenda_items.title: Early Learning and Pre-K Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy, Dr. Suzanne Cotterman, and Durham PreK's Linda Chappell presented DPS early learning strategies, online and multilingual ESL enrollment outreach, and special/blended classroom growth from 61 classrooms (784 seats) to 65 classrooms (858 seats) in 2021-22 and 68 classrooms (914 seats) in 2022-23 at Lyons Farm Elementary. Officials also discussed incorporating Pre-K spaces into new school designs such as Elementary F, Child Find evaluations, equity assessment recommendations, and wraparound before- and after-care gaps.

agenda_items.title: DPS School Year and Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS CFO Paul LeSieur thanked commissioners for over $11 million in new annual county funding—bringing total county support to $169 million, including $5.6 million for operations, $6 million for capital outlay, $500,000 for English learners, $250 certified staff supplement raises toward $5,600, and added custodial/counselor/equity positions, while noting roughly $31 million passes through to charter schools. LeSieur outlined pending state House/Senate budget differences (2.5-2.6% raises vs. Governor's 5%, ~22.8% retirement, >$7,000 health insurance, $15/hour minimum wage phase-in, and $15 million in potential technology forfeiture funds), and members discussed avoiding the 20% charter pass-through on Pre-K requests, $2 million hotspot costs, and school nurse vacancies.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) and 2022 GO Bond Referendum Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane reviewed broadband ARPA/federal strategy and the FY22-FY31 10-year CIP update, noting half of the county's $60-70 million annual debt service supports DPS and warning of 20-80% construction cost inflation (100% steel and 375% lumber spikes) and supply/labor constraints. Lane walked through milestones leading to a November 8, 2022 General Obligation bond referendum, and officials discussed updating DPS facility needs, $40,000 in county funding added to The Institute's contract for MWBE construction outreach, carbon-reduction investments, and property tax rate pressures.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments Check, COVID-19 Reopening Coordination, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer confirmed no citizens had signed up or submitted emails for public comment. DPS Chair Bettina Umstead thanked the county for its mask mandate, and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga requested Sheriff's Office and City traffic support during the first two weeks of school and expanded 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. community COVID-19 testing sites before BOCC Chair Howerton noted the November 16, 2021 joint meeting and adjourned at 11:00 a.m.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 12, 2021 5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 12, 2021 work session presided over by Natalie Beyer (with Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis absent from all roll calls), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education approved its agenda, June 10, 2021 work session minutes, and—following extensive public comment and board debate—adopted 2021-22 return-to-school COVID-19 health and safety protocols 6-0. Parents and People's Alliance advocates urged weekly surveillance testing, staff vaccine reporting, quarantine continuity, and outdoor dining due to the Delta variant, prompting board members Matt Sears, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Natalie Beyer, and Bettina Umstead to push for outdoor lunch priority and testing/vaccine incentives, while Dr. Mike Lee cautioned against forcing students outdoors during extreme heat, rain, or cold. The board proceeded with staff's flexible cafeteria/classroom/outdoor recommendations as presented. The board also heard a legal and demographic redistricting presentation from attorney Deborah Stagner and demographer Blake Esselstyn using newly released 2020 Census data showing Durham County's population at 324,833 and Districts 2A and 4B outside the plus-or-minus 5% deviation threshold, unanimously approving up to $17,500 for redistricting services before entering closed session and approving the August 12 personnel report.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Concluding an agenda roll-call vote (captured on stream with Matt Sears and presiding member Natalie Beyer voting Aye), the board next considered the June 10, 2021 work session minutes. Recommendations included universal indoor masking, 3-foot student distancing, bus seating charts, daily disinfecting, opting into NCDHHS K-12 testing, Ignite Online Academy updates (>700 enrolled, enrollment closed), and flexible cafeteria/classroom/outdoor meals. Board members debated prioritizing outdoor dining versus weather/site constraints and volunteer vaccination rules before adopting the staff recommendations 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Board of Education Electoral Redistricting Presentation and Contract Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni introduced Tharrington Smith attorney Deborah Stagner and demographer Blake Esselstyn to present decennial school board redistricting requirements under one-person, one-vote and Voting Rights Act standards. Using 2020 Census data released earlier that day (total county population 324,833; ideal single-district population ~81,208), Esselstyn reported that Districts 1A and 3B remained within plus-or-minus 5% deviation while Districts 2A (below -5%) and 4B (above +5%) require line adjustments. disagreements.issue: Cafeteria Reopening vs. Prioritizing Outdoor Lunch and Amending Reopening Motion Language
disagreements.summary: During review of the 2021-22 COVID-19 reopening plan, board members diverged on how strongly to mandate or prioritize outdoor dining over indoor cafeterias and whether to formally amend staff's cafeteria recommendation slide before voting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prioritize outdoor eating with tents/shade and explicitly move outdoor-meal language ahead of indoor cafeteria reinstatement in the board's approved recommendations.
side_a_arguments: Unmasked indoor eating in crowded cafeterias poses heightened Delta-variant transmission risk for unvaccinated K-6 students.
Leading the recommendation slide with reinstating cafeterias sends the wrong signal to families and principals unless outdoor options are emphasized first or formally amended.
disagreements.side_b_position: Preserve principal/school-site flexibility across cafeterias, classrooms, and outdoor spaces without requiring outdoor lunch in harsh weather or amending the recommendation text.
side_b_arguments: Not every child is comfortable eating outdoors during extreme summer heat, rain, or freezing winter weather, and accommodations are needed for indoor options.
Not all school campuses or facilities can immediately accommodate full outdoor dining, and the recommendation already encourages outdoor space weather permitting.
disagreements.resolution: After administration confirmed schools already had flexibility across cafeterias, classrooms, and outdoors—and noted DPS Foundation grants were funding outdoor tents—the board agreed to proceed with the unamended motion while committing to support principals with outdoor learning and eating resources, passing the plan 6-0.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting June 24, 2021 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 24, 2021 monthly meeting, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved its consent agenda—including the Duke Trauma-Informed Leadership Teams (TILT) and Capturing Kids' Hearts contracts—and finalized its multi-year policy manual transition by adopting Policies 1910 (District Improvement and Performance Reports) and 4342 (Student Searches) while rescinding the legacy policy manual. Following an amendment by Natalie Beyer to advocate alongside the Durham community for funding, the board also unanimously adopted Policy 1900, its landmark Racial and Educational Equity Policy. During public comment, speakers addressed COVID-19 learning loss and August masking, criticized the downsized Northern High School theater design, praised the board's resolution opposing House Bill 324, and presented student data on racial disparities in in-school suspensions at Durham School of the Arts while backing the non-renewal of its former principal. In a major policy clash, administration's proposal to outsource substitute teacher management to Kelly Education Services drew bipartisan-style pushback from board members over privatization, lower-tier contractor benefits, and lack of teacher/substitute input, resulting in deferral for stakeholder engagement; the board also reviewed the district's Social and Emotional Learning and Mental Health Improvement Plan before entering closed session and approving the June 24 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Amended Agenda Approval, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the monthly meeting with interpreters Martha Romo Aguiles and Marty Ramirez and led a moment of silence honoring educators for finishing the pandemic school year and launching summer learning. Natalie Beyer moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded approving the agenda as amended to add a Superintendent's Update (7-0), in which Dr. Pascal Mubenga celebrated full in-person graduations and roughly $40 million in senior scholarships.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 20, 2021 Monthly Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the minutes from its May 20, 2021 monthly meeting. Alexandra Valladares moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval with no changes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community speakers addressed pandemic recovery and August masking, urged DPS to publicly acknowledge and fix theater/stage downsizing in the new Northern High School design (Irving Truitt, Sharon Campbell, Wendell Tabb), and praised the board's resolution opposing House Bill 324 (anti-CRT legislation, Renee Rachel Galper). Durham School of the Arts students/graduates (Amon Abdul-Malik, Jay Rahim, Katie Mungal) and Dan McKinney (Organizing Against Racism Durham) presented data showing 1,493 in-school suspensions issued to 385 DSA students in 2018-19 (80% non-white), urged eliminating zero-tolerance discipline and forming a student advocacy board, and backed the non-renewal of former DSA principal David Hawks.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The consent agenda covered the Board Policies Transition Project, Lakewood Montessori Middle School foundation repairs (L.A. Downey & Son Inc.), Lyons Farm Elementary sanitary sewer easements, the Trauma-Informed Leadership Teams (TILT) contract with the Center for Child and Family Health, the Capturing Kids' Hearts contract, an Education-Based Services agreement, Home School Policy 3103, and a Serenic software extension. Frederick Xavier Ravin III asked for public highlights on the TILT contract, which staff agreed to fold into the later mental health presentation, and the consent agenda passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Chief of Staff: Board Policy Manual Transition (Policies 1910 & 4342) and Sunset of Old Manual
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment from Wendell Tabb seeking revisions to field-trip Policy 3320 on pre-approval, vaccination travel hurdles, and insurance consistency, Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni, Dr. Julie Spencer, and Tina Ingram presented second-reading updates to Policy 1910 (renamed District Improvement and Performance Reports) and Policy 4342 (Student Searches, reframed with welcoming/safe climate language), plus full rescission of the legacy policy manual. Board members discussed Spanish policy translation via BoardDocs and requested a summary list of legacy policies not carried forward before voting 7-0 to adopt both policies and sunset the old manual.

agenda_items.title: Policy 1900: Racial and Educational Equity Policy (Second Reading & Adoption)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Executive Director of Equity Affairs Dr. Daniel Kelvin Bullock and Tanya Giovanni presented second-draft revisions to Policy 1900, reordering pillars to elevate Social and Emotional Learning, changing pillar verbs to action imperatives (Disrupt, Dismantle, Build, Honor, Strengthen), adding resource-advocacy language, and removing an interim restorative-practices definition to co-develop one with the community honoring Indigenous origins. Matt Sears moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded adoption, Natalie Beyer moved a unanimously approved amendment to add 'advocate with the Durham community,' and the board adopted Policy 1900 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Human Resources: Kelly Education Services Substitute Teacher Staffing Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR Chief Dr. Alvera Lesane, CFO Paul LeSieur, and Kelly Education Services representatives Ben Davis and Bobby Shore proposed outsourcing substitute teacher management to Kelly under a 30-day evergreen contract promising weekly pay, $15+/hour rates, ACA benefit options, 5-day/week schedules, and $80,000-$100,000 projected savings to raise the 68-75% fill rate toward 95%. Board members Matt Sears, Natalie Beyer, Alexandra Valladares, and Frederick Xavier Ravin III raised concerns over privatization precedents, Kelly's 1.3x markup and lower-tier health plans, alternatives such as an internal full-time sub pool or biweekly payroll outsourcing, and missing time-cost data and educator input, leading administration to defer the proposal for teacher, principal, and substitute feedback.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Deferred / Returned to staff for stakeholder engagement (No vote)

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Social and Emotional Learning and Mental Health Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy, James Futrell, Dr. Christopher Soto, and Dr. Laverne Maddox-Perry presented DPS's MTSS-aligned Social and Emotional Learning and Mental Health Improvement Plan, highlighting elementary SEL curricula, the Embrace Calm hub, Shape assessments, universal screeners, staff training, and the TILT trauma-informed partnership with the Duke Center for Child and Family Health across 22 elementary schools and one middle school. Natalie Beyer welcomed educator flexibility to choose Responsive Classroom over Capturing Kids' Hearts, noting criticisms that the latter focuses on behavioral management rather than trauma-informed care.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and June 24, 2021 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously by voice vote to enter closed session at 03:02:10. Returning to open session at 03:37:10, Natalie Beyer moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded approval of the June 24, 2021 personnel report as discussed in closed session, passing 7-0 before adjournment.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting June 24, 2021 6:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Outsourcing Substitute Teacher Staffing to Kelly Education Services
disagreements.summary: Administration proposed contracting substitute teacher management to third-party vendor Kelly Education Services to improve low fill rates and offer weekly pay and ACA benefit options, while multiple board members pushed back sharply over privatization precedents, vendor markup and benefit quality, and missing stakeholder consultation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Partner with Kelly Education Services under a 30-day evergreen contract to provide weekly pay, 5-day workweeks, ACA benefits, and dedicated placement support for substitutes.
side_a_arguments: Substitute fill rates fell to 68% in 2019-21 (75% five-year average), disrupting classrooms and forcing teachers and principals to cover uncovered classes.
State health plan and ACA/retiree rules bar DPS from offering standard state benefits or weekly payroll to non-permanent substitutes without costly HR/payroll staffing and Serenic software changes.
Kelly charges no upfront fee, projects $80,000-$100,000 in district savings, preserves DPS's $15+/hour pay rate, and could raise fill rates toward 95%.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer action on outsourcing and examine in-house alternatives, full labor/cost analysis, and direct input from substitutes, teachers, and principals before privatizing substitute positions.
side_b_arguments: The board recently went through a difficult process bringing custodial staff back in-house and is wary of setting a precedent for privatizing public school roles or relying on a vendor's 1.3x markup and inferior private health plans.

No actual contract was included in the packet, and staff had not quantified central-office/treasurer labor savings or explored hiring a smaller 50-75 full-time internal sub pool or contracting out biweekly payroll alone.
The board needed direct feedback from classroom teachers, principals, and current substitutes before changing their employment status.
disagreements.resolution: Seeing strong board unreadiness and unanswered questions, HR Chief Dr. Alvera Lesane agreed to pause the proposal and convene stakeholder sessions with teachers, principals, and substitutes before bringing it back to the board.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Retreat June 17, 2021 8:30 AM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its annual full-day retreat on June 17, 2021 at the Minnie Forte-Brown Staff Development Center, chaired by Bettina Umstead with no formal votes taken. In the morning academic session, Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy and staff presented 'Growing Together' equity groundwork toward a fall 2021 elementary magnet policy revision, reviewing 2021 lottery acceptance data, diversity-oriented magnet integration strategies, and regional gaps in Pre-K and Exceptional Children (EC) autism classrooms. In the afternoon operations session, board members urged aggressive teacher supplement increases, affordable teacher housing exploration, and higher pay for classified staff and bus drivers to stay competitive with neighboring districts, GoTriangle, and the City of Durham ($22/hour). Staff also reviewed Level 2 custodial cleaning standards, layering Pre-K/EC spaces onto the $500 million-plus Capital Improvement Program and $6 million annual county CIP, fall 2021 attendance boundary work, and statutory K-3 class-size ratios.

agenda_items.title: Welcome and Retreat Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the June 17 retreat at the Minnie Forte-Brown Staff Development Center around the theme 'Growing Together.' Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga framed the day's structure, dedicating the morning to academics and the afternoon to operations.

agenda_items.title: Growing Together: Elementary Magnet Policy Revision and Pre-K/EC Alignment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy, Dr. Pippen, Matthew Palmer, Ms. Cooper, and Ms. Marshall reviewed 18 months of work toward fall 2021 magnet policy adoption, seeking board guidance via scenario exercises. Staff presented an inventory of Pre-K and EC classrooms across regions—noting seven Pre-K autism classrooms district-wide with one large high school region lacking any—and asked whether specialized classrooms belong in neighborhood or choice/magnet schools, alongside 2021 lottery data and research on diversity-oriented magnets.

agenda_items.title: Staff Compensation, Teacher Supplements, Bus Driver Pay, and Community Engagement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During afternoon strategic plan discussions, board members warned DPS was falling behind two adjoining districts on teacher supplements, flagged rising local housing costs and affordable teacher housing, and urged revisiting the $15/hour classified wage floor ahead of the next county budget cycle. Members also noted GoTriangle and City of Durham bus driver recruitment at $22/hour; staff reported working with Paul LeSieur and Mr. Modesto to provide bus drivers an increase this year, and highlighted parent ambassador and school perception initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Priority 5 Operations: Custodial Standards, Capital Improvement Program, and K-3 Class Sizes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julie Spencer and Dr. Julius Monk (with Dr. Anderson) reviewed Level 2 custodial cleaning standards and equipment capital replacement planning. Staff highlighted the $500 million-plus CIP and $6 million annual CIP approved by County Commissioners, nearly $3 million across ~70 lottery-funded projects, an upcoming August financial update layering Pre-K and EC rooms onto the 2019 facility condition assessment, fall 2021 attendance boundary work, and statutory K-3 class-size caps (18 in kindergarten, 16 in first grade, 17 in second and third).

agenda_items.title: Closing Remarks and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy, Chair Bettina Umstead, Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis, and board members thanked staff for preparing the interactive retreat ahead of Operation Summer Learning and July school openings before adjourning.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session June 10, 2021 5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 10, 2021 work session presided over by Chair Bettina Umstead with six board members voting in the recorded afternoon/evening action votes, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard over an hour of sharply divided public comment regarding the non-renewal of Durham School of the Arts Principal David Hawks' contract—with supporters praising his 14-year tenure and special-education/EL outcomes while alumni and equity advocates cited defensive responses to student racism complaints and urged stakeholder inclusion in selecting the next principal. The board reviewed consent items including Carrington Middle School wireless, Elementary School F construction management, and indoor air quality consulting. The board unanimously approved the 2021-22 alternative school modified accountability model, advanced Policy 3103 (requiring at least half-time enrollment for homeschool/private students to use DPS courses or activities) on first reading 6-0, and renewed Durham Technical Community College trustees John Burness and Rev. Michael Page 6-0 after discussing whether future trustee seats should be openly solicited. Following closed session, the board unanimously approved the June 10, 2021 personnel report before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment on Durham School of the Arts Leadership
agenda_items.discussion_summary: More than a dozen students, alumni, parents, teachers, and PTSA leaders spoke on the departure of Durham School of the Arts (DSA) Principal David Hawks. DSA PTSA outgoing co-president Laura Kagan urged a transparent principal search involving diverse students, parents, and faculty, while speakers including teacher Anthony Amos II, retired teacher Jody Kraft, Rosanna Morgan, and Jenny Surface praised Hawks' 14-year record, support for students with disabilities and LEP, and personal compassion; meanwhile, DSA alumni Aman Abdul-Malik and Jay Rahaim and other community speakers detailed unaddressed 2020 student equity complaints, a stalled Student Bill of Rights update, and traumatic student experiences.

agenda_items.title: Consent Items Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board took up Item 6 consent items covering Carrington Middle School wireless upgrades, Elementary School F construction management, and an indoor air quality program management consultation services agreement (subsequent discussion/vote occurs in the truncated middle segment).

agenda_items.title: 2021-22 Alternative School Modified Accountability Model
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following academic services presentation celebrating alternative school student growth, Bettina Umstead moved and Alexandra Valladares seconded approving the 2021-22 alternative school modified accountability model, which passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Policy 3103 (Use of Educational Services and Resources / Half-Time Enrollment) First Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Spencer, Dr. Nikia Hardy, Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni, and Erin Smith presented proposed Policy 3103 for first reading, requiring homeschool or private school students to enroll at least half-time in DPS (per the NCDPI attendance manual) to access DPS courses, co-curriculars, and extracurriculars, qualifying them for ADM funding and DPS graduation while aligning with Policies 3101 and 3620. Board members discussed CTE introductory access and enrollment logistics before voting 6-0 on a motion by Bettina Umstead seconded by Natalie Beyer to advance the policy to second reading at the June board meeting.

agenda_items.title: Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed two expiring DPS-appointed seats on the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees held by DTCC Board Chair John Burness and Rev. Michael Page, both of whom sought reappointment amid DTCC's strategic planning process. After questioning whether the board should solicit outside applicants, Frederick Xavier Ravin III moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded renewing both appointees' terms, passing 6-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Summary of Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Follow-up items included forming a policy review committee on student searches and data dashboards, examining equity policy evaluation metrics and restorative practice definitions, supporting special needs, marketing, deferred needs, and health department nursing/supervisor roles in the budget, and refining Policy 3103 implementation and full-time enrollment incentives. The board entered closed session unanimously and reconvened at 05:20:22 to unanimously approve the June 10, 2021 personnel report on a motion by Natalie Beyer seconded by Bettina Umstead.
