meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOCC/BOE Quarterly Meeting May 18, 2021 9:00 AM
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 18, 2021 joint quarterly meeting of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education and the Durham Board of County Commissioners presided over by DPS Chair Bettina Umstead, the two boards unanimously approved revised February 16, 2021 joint meeting minutes (adding a member omitted from attendance). Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane presented the FY21-22 Manager's Recommended Budget, proposing a 1-cent property tax increase (to 72.22 cents per $100 valuation) and $163.3 million in DPS funding—a 6.6% increase adding $8.9 million in current expense (including $1.9 million to sustain the $15/hour classified wage floor) and $1.13 million in capital outlay. In reviewing a draft joint Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) presented by DPS members Jovonia Lewis and Frederick Xavier Ravin III, officials debated inter-board communication protocols, aligning county budget performance metrics with DPS's strategic and racial equity plans, moving the DPS budget request deadline from mid-March to April 1, and creating a budget indexing formula. After County Budget Director Keith Lane warned that an April 1 deadline falls too late to synchronize with county department requests, Chair Umstead agreed to revert the draft MOU date to mid-March pending agreement from Lewis and Ravin, and officials requested joint staff review of the indexing proposal before finalizing the MOU next quarter.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of February 16, 2021 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Chair Bettina Umstead called the virtual joint BOCC/BOE meeting to order and reviewed the agenda. Following a board member's request to correct the February 16, 2021 joint meeting minutes to reflect her attendance, County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved approval with the correction (seconded by another Commissioner), passing unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Durham County FY21-22 Manager's Recommended Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane reported $19.7 million in projected general fund natural revenue growth ($13.6M property tax, $6.1M sales tax) and $2.2 billion in tax base growth, proposing a 1-cent property tax rate increase from 71.22 to 72.22 cents per $100 valuation (~$4.58M-$4.6M total, or $20/year on a $200,000 home). The recommended budget allocates $163.3 million to Durham Public Schools—a 6.6% increase consisting of $8.9 million in new current expense funding (including $1.9 million to sustain $15/hour classified pay) and $1.13 million in new capital funding (raising capital outlay from $3.37M to $4.5M).

agenda_items.title: Joint BOCC/BOE Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Revisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members Jovonia Lewis and Frederick Xavier Ravin III presented proposed updates to the BOCC/BOE MOU: avoiding unilateral commissioner political statements after joint meetings ('we don't answer to you, but we work with you'), aligning county budget narrative metrics with DPS's Strategic Plan, Racial Equity Action Plan (with Dr. Kelvin Bullock), EC priorities, and student climate surveys, shifting DPS's draft budget submission to April 1, and exploring a transparent budget indexing formula. County Budget Director Keith Lane objected to the April 1 deadline as too late for county budget compilation, prompting Chair Umstead to offer reverting to mid-March, while a member urged a year of staff study on indexing before locking boards into a formula.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Deferred to next quarterly meeting

votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; moved by BOCC Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and seconded by an unidentified County Commissioner.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOCC/BOE Quarterly Meeting May 18, 2021 9:00 AM
disagreements.issue: DPS Budget Request Submission Deadline (April 1 vs. Mid-March) in Joint MOU
disagreements.summary: DPS MOU drafters proposed moving the school board's annual draft budget request to the county from mid-March to April 1, while County Budget Director Keith Lane urged keeping the mid-March timeline.
disagreements.side_a_position: Move the DPS draft budget request deadline in the joint MOU from mid-March to April 1.
side_a_arguments: Aligns the school district's budget preparation with the county's budget development cycle.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain the mid-March deadline for DPS's initial budget request.
side_b_arguments: DPS funding is by far the county's largest budget allocation, and April 1 arrives after all other county department requests are already being compiled.
Moving two weeks later prevents county budget staff from comparing DPS needs alongside other county departments.
disagreements.resolution: After County Budget Director Keith Lane raised the timing concern, Chair Bettina Umstead agreed to amend the draft MOU back to the earlier mid-March date pending sign-off by Jovonia Lewis and Frederick Xavier Ravin III ahead of the next quarterly meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOCC/BOE Quarterly Meeting May 18, 2021 9:00 AM
disagreements.issue: Proposed Budget Indexing Formula in Joint BOCC/BOE MOU
disagreements.summary: Frederick Xavier Ravin III and the draft MOU proposed exploring a budget indexing formula for DPS funding, while another official cautioned against locking boards into a rigid formula without staff study.
disagreements.side_a_position: Establish a working indexing formula in the MOU to project expected school system funding needs.
side_a_arguments: Creates a more transparent and predictable budget development process for both boards and staff.
disagreements.side_b_position: Have mutual budget staffs thoroughly review or study any indexing formula for a year before adopting it.
side_b_arguments: Locking into a formula could prevent the boards from having deep, responsive discussions as community needs change.
disagreements.resolution: Deferred for joint budget staff review and feedback before finalizing the MOU at the next quarterly meeting.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session May 6, 2021 5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 6, 2021 work session presided over by Matt Sears (with six board members voting on recorded 6-0 voice votes), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education amended its agenda 6-0 to add a supplemental marketing/engagement funding item proposed by Bettina Umstead and an anti-transgender legislation opposition resolution proposed by Natalie Beyer, and approved two sets of work session minutes 6-0. Nineteen written public comments addressed holding magnet seats for Ignite virtual learners at George Watts, Pre-K/elementary Spanish instruction, reducing i-Ready testing, DCABP calls for accountability at Durham School of the Arts, removing weapons from schools, and Durham Association of Educators demands for 50 new school nurse and social worker positions rather than the two nurses proposed by administration. Later in the session, Dr. Nakia Hardy and Dr. Laverne Maddox-Perry presented a new policy allowing high school students to repeat courses for grade replacement alongside retention review hearings. Following questions from Frederick Xavier Ravin III on lowering electronic/parental barriers for retention reviews and Natalie Beyer's request for a post-summer report, the board voted unanimously to waive second reading and adopt the policy before entering closed session and approving the May 6 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Work Session Chair Matt Sears called the meeting to order, recognized interpreters Martha Romo-Aguiles and Marty Ramirez, and led a moment of silence for global pandemic struggles. The board voted 6-0 to add Item 7A (supplemental marketing and engagement funding, moved by Bettina Umstead and seconded by Natalie Beyer) and Item 8D (resolution opposing proposed discriminatory and anti-transgender legislation, moved by Natalie Beyer), and then approved two sets of work session minutes 6-0 on a motion by Natalie Beyer seconded by Frederick Xavier Ravin III.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Nineteen online public comments were read aloud at one minute each (no in-person speakers). Multiple speakers—including Nina Pandey, Jessica Womack, Nicholas Graber-Grace, and Vanessa Barnett-Loro—urged adding 50 school nurse and social worker positions using federal COVID relief and county reserves rather than only two nurses in Dr. Mubenga's proposed budget; others sought George Watts magnet seat holds for virtual learners until children are vaccinated, elementary Spanish, less standardized testing, weapon-free schools, and DCABP truth-telling and accountability regarding leadership at Durham School of the Arts.

agenda_items.title: Course Repeat for Grade Replacement and Retention Review Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Dr. Laverne Maddox-Perry presented a policy allowing students to repeat courses for numeric grade replacement (distinct from P/F credit recovery) via NCVPS or traditional classes to aid post-pandemic recovery, requesting waiver of second reading for summer 2021 rollout. Frederick Xavier Ravin III questioned the three-day written retention review window in Section D1 and urged a simple online/phone workflow to reduce parent barriers, while Natalie Beyer asked about elementary/middle school retention risks and requested a post-summer update; on Beyer's motion seconded by Alexandra Valladares, the board unanimously waived second reading and adopted the policy.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, and May 6, 2021 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Follow-up items included developing metrics to evaluate the marketing campaign, incorporating Ignite board feedback into final staff recommendations, providing a fall opening update including culturally affirmative learning spaces, and creating an accessible electronic retention-review workflow. meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Emergency Meeting April 14,  2021 3:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At a virtual emergency called meeting on April 14, 2021 presided over by Chair Bettina Umstead (with Matt Sears absent/unresponsive on roll calls), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved the agenda 6-0 and voted 6-0 by roll call to approve an emergency sole-source contract with Comfort Mechanical Contractors to replace the failed, irreparable water-cooled chiller at Durham School of the Arts (DSA). Dr. Julius Monk explained that losing the chiller prevented cooling and COVID-19 ventilation/filtration across DSA's main and science buildings, invoking the N.C.G.S. 143-129(e)(2) health-and-safety emergency bidding exception to secure an in-stock unit within roughly three weeks rather than waiting until November. Dr. Mike Lee, Natalie Beyer, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, and Alexandra Valladares sharply criticized Durham County Commissioners for years of underfunding deferred capital needs—noting cuts to the 2016 school bond from $190 million to $90 million, denied 2018 and 2020 bonds, HVAC failures at Parkwood, Morehead, and other campuses, and fewer than 10 HVAC technicians maintaining 6 million square feet—and urged charging the cost to capital funds and presenting upcoming system risks at the May joint meeting.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the 3:30 p.m. emergency virtual meeting to order and led a moment of silence. On a motion by Dr. Mike Lee seconded by Natalie Beyer, the board approved the agenda 6-0 by roll call, with Matt Sears absent/not responding.

agenda_items.title: Durham School of the Arts Emergency Replacement of Water-Cooled Chiller Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk and Dr. Anderson reported that DSA's remaining chiller failed irreparably, leaving the main and science buildings without cooling or COVID-19 ventilation standards, and recommended contracting immediately with Comfort Mechanical Contractors under N.C.G.S. 143-129(e)(2) so an in-stock chiller could ship and be installed in roughly three weeks. Board members Dr. Mike Lee, Natalie Beyer, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, and Alexandra Valladares condemned repeated county deferrals of DPS capital needs—highlighting 2016/2018/2020 bond cuts and active monitoring of 3 failed and 15 strained HVAC campuses—before voting 6-0 by roll call (motion by Jovonia Lewis, second by Natalie Beyer) to approve the emergency contract.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Meeting  March 2 , 2021  5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Reconvening its February 25 meeting on March 2, 2021 under Chair Bettina Umstead, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved its agenda and heard translated Spanish-language public comments alongside 30 minutes drawn from 225 new public submissions sharply divided over March 15 school reopening following the failed legislative override of Senate Bill 37. The board then resumed debate on Matt Sears's tabled motion (seconded by Natalie Beyer) to push back in-person reopening for all schools to April 8, 2021 after spring break. In a 3-4 roll-call split vote, the motion failed: Matt Sears, Natalie Beyer, and Alexandra Valladares voted Aye to delay reopening until April 8 for additional staff vaccination time and calendar alignment, while Bettina Umstead, Jovonia Lewis, Dr. Mike Lee, and Frederick Xavier Ravin III voted Nay to preserve the March 15 elementary reopening schedule. Following the vote, board members requested written clarity on staff accommodations, vaccine robocalls, and six-foot Plan B social distancing compliance before moving toward in-person board meetings on March 11.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the reconvened March 2, 2021 meeting (recessed from February 25) to order and led a moment of silence. Natalie Beyer moved and Dr. Mike Lee and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded approving the agenda, which passed 7-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment (Including Translated Spanish Submissions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Communications Officer Chip Sudderth read Spanish-language public comments held over from February 25 and then read 30-second excerpts for 30 minutes from 225 newly submitted comments. Commenters split between urging the board to hold firm on March 15 reopening and expand outdoor athletics spectatorship versus demanding a delay following the failed SB 37 veto override until staff were vaccinated and strict CDC six-foot spacing could be met.

agenda_items.title: Reopening Start Date Reconsideration: Motion to Open All Schools April 8, 2021
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board resumed debate on Matt Sears's tabled motion (seconded by Natalie Beyer) to move in-person reopening for all schools to April 8, 2021 after spring break. Sears, Beyer, and Alexandra Valladares favored the delay to reduce community division and give staff more time for vaccinations and planning, whereas Bettina Umstead, Jovonia Lewis, Dr. Mike Lee, and Frederick Xavier Ravin III cited first-dose immunity data, declining positivity rates, and student needs in voting to keep March 15; the motion failed 3-4 by roll call. Afterward, members discussed verifying six-foot distancing in elementary schools, sending vaccine robocalls, clarifying accommodations, and resuming in-person board meetings on March 11.

votes.notes: Split 3-4 roll call vote; Chair Bettina Umstead voted last against the motion ('It's time for our district to move back March 15th') and confirmed the motion failed.
votes.discussion_detail: Matt Sears restated his tabled motion from February 25 (seconded by Natalie Beyer) to open all schools on April 8, 2021 following spring break. disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Meeting  March 2 , 2021  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Delaying In-Person Reopening to April 8 vs. Keeping March 15 Elementary Start Date
disagreements.summary: Following the failed Senate Bill 37 veto override, the board split 3-4 on whether to delay all in-person reopening until April 8, 2021 (after spring break) or proceed with the previously approved March 15 elementary reopening schedule.
disagreements.side_a_position: Delay in-person reopening for all schools until April 8, 2021 after spring break.
side_a_arguments: Provide teachers and staff additional time for COVID-19 vaccinations and second-dose protection before returning to classrooms.
Heal community division and give principals and families clear written answers on Plan B six-foot spacing and staff accommodations.
Align reopening with a post-spring-break transition rather than a mid-March disruption.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain the March 15, 2021 elementary reopening timeline.
side_b_arguments: First-dose vaccination studies showed strong partial protection (~92% cited) and local positivity rates had dropped from January peaks.
Students struggling academically and emotionally in remote instruction needed timely access to in-person learning options.
Staff accommodations for ADA and high COVID risk could cover the virtual teaching positions needed without delaying reopening.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to move reopening to April 8 failed 3-4 on roll call at 01:48:49, keeping the March 15 elementary reopening date in place.

meetings.executive_summary: At a February 18, 2021 emergency called meeting presided over by Chair Bettina Umstead, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously adopted its agenda 7-0 and reviewed administration's proposed in-person learning timeline amid pending General Assembly Senate Bill 37. Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga and staff outlined returning elementary teachers on March 8 and elementary students on March 15 in a three-cohort hybrid model (with a 100% virtual option), followed by middle and high school after spring break. Following intense debate over community COVID-19 positivity (7-8%), educator vaccine access, and whether to wait on Governor Cooper's action on SB 37, Dr. Mike Lee's motion to adopt the proposed reopening timeline passed 5-2 by roll call: Dr. Mike Lee, Jovonia Lewis, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Alexandra Valladares, and Bettina Umstead voted Aye, while Matt Sears and Natalie Beyer voted Nay.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the emergency meeting to order and led a moment of silence. Natalie Beyer moved and Matt Sears seconded approving the agenda, which passed 7-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Presentation and Vote on In-Person Learning Options and Reopening Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga and senior staff presented a reopening plan under Plan A/B featuring a three-cohort rotation and 100% virtual option, proposing elementary staff return March 8, elementary students return March 15, and secondary students follow after spring break (April 8/15) while navigating potential 15-day compliance deadlines under Senate Bill 37. Board members divided over whether to act immediately or delay until more staff received second vaccine doses and SB 37's fate was settled, before passing Dr. Mike Lee's motion adopting the staff reopening timeline 5-2 by roll call.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Emergency Meeting  February 18, 2021  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Adopting March 15 Elementary Reopening Timeline vs. Delaying for Full Staff Vaccination and SB 37 Action
disagreements.summary: Board members split 5-2 over whether to commit immediately to administration's March 15 elementary reopening schedule (and post-spring break secondary reopening) or delay reopening until educators received full two-dose vaccination immunity and Governor Cooper acted on Senate Bill 37.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the March 15 elementary and post-spring-break secondary reopening timeline immediately regardless of SB 37's final status.
side_a_arguments: The board should take ownership of its reopening decision rather than deferring to state legislators or awaiting a potential veto.
Student mental health and learning struggles under prolonged Plan C required offering an in-person option for families who want it.
Initiating ~1,000 educator vaccinations per week alongside contact tracing, PPE, and school-closure protocols provided sufficient mitigation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay reopening or make the March 15 date contingent on SB 37 becoming law to allow full vaccination and a cleaner academic break.
side_b_arguments: Community positivity remained near 7-8% (above the board's 4% metric) with emerging variants, and educators were weeks away from full two-dose protection.
March 15 was driven by General Assembly SB 37 deadlines rather than a natural academic quarter break.
Waiting a week or tying the timeline to a gubernatorial veto would allow teacher feedback and a more logical calendar date.
disagreements.resolution: Dr. Mike Lee's motion adopting the March 15 elementary / post-spring-break secondary reopening timeline passed 5-2 by roll call at 02:07:01.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education with The Durham Delegation  January 29, 2021  5:00 - 6:30
meetings.executive_summary: At a virtual legislative roundtable on January 29, 2021 hosted by Chair Bettina Umstead, six Durham Public Schools Board of Education members (Bettina Umstead, Jovonia Lewis, Dr. Mike Lee, Natalie Beyer, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, and Alexandra Valladares) and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga met with Durham's General Assembly delegation—Reps. Vernetta Alston, Marcia Morey, and Zack Hawkins, and Sens. Mike Woodard and Natalie Murdock—to align on 2021 legislative priorities. Dr. Mubenga outlined four urgent priorities including pandemic learning-loss funding, school calendar flexibility, enrollment hold-harmless relief after losing roughly 2% (~1,700 students), and competitive school nurse salaries. Sen. Woodard inquired about DPS's ~$750 million capital needs backlog ahead of potential state infrastructure bond discussions, while board members and legislators discussed behavioral/mental health partnerships (such as DHHS and YMCA collaborations) instead of punitive discipline, educator diversity pipelines, and reforming A-F school accountability letter grades. No formal motions or votes were taken during the informational advocacy session.

agenda_items.title: Welcome and Introductions of DPS Board and Durham Legislative Delegation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead welcomed state lawmakers Reps. Vernetta Alston, Marcia Morey, and Zack Hawkins and Sens. Mike Woodard and Natalie Murdock alongside DPS board members (Umstead, Lewis, Lee, Beyer, Ravin, and Valladares) and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga. Participants introduced themselves and their districts ahead of reviewing DPS's 2021 legislative priorities.

agenda_items.title: Urgent Legislative Priorities: Learning Loss, Calendar Flexibility, Enrollment, and School Nurses
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga highlighted pandemic learning loss, local school calendar flexibility to align with community colleges, enrollment hold-harmless protections after losing roughly 2% (~1,700 students), and salary flexibility to recruit school nurses amid hospital competition. Lawmakers noted early state budget negotiations, federal PPE funds, and strong support for addressing enrollment and nurse staffing needs.

agenda_items.title: State Infrastructure Bond, $750M Capital Backlog, and Student Mental Health Partnerships
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In response to Sen. Mike Woodard's question on state school construction bond needs, Dr. Mubenga reported a ~$750 million capital needs assessment (~$250 million short even with ~$500 million in 10-year county commitments for three school rebuilds). Board members and Sen. Natalie Murdock also discussed educator diversity pipelines, professional development, mental and behavioral health supports with DHHS and nonprofit partners, and avoiding punitive discipline for young students.

agenda_items.title: Accountability Testing, A-F School Grades, and Quarterly Delegation Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members criticized A-F school performance grades and standardized test incentives for penalizing schools serving EC and ESL learners and urged growth-based accountability. Lawmakers thanked Jovonia Lewis for sharing the social studies standards resolution, pledged bipartisan bridge-building, and agreed to hold quarterly check-ins to advance shared education priorities before Chair Umstead adjourned.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session  January 14, 2021  5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 14, 2021 monthly work session presided over by Frederick Xavier Ravin III, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved (7-0) its amended agenda (adding a draft legislative agenda review), the amended December 2, 2020 work session minutes, the consent agenda (including the quarterly construction change order log and FY2019-20 Budget Amendment #4), and the Construction Management at Risk delivery method for 2020 capital improvement projects to expand MWBE subcontractor participation. After a truncated middle section covering elementary design consultant recommendations and a $15/hour minimum wage update, the board unanimously adopted (7-0) resolutions proclaiming January 2021 National Mentoring Month and honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Because an online poll for the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force initially listed only one option, the board voted 7-0 to extend applications to January 22 and postpone the task force selection vote to January 28, reviewed its draft 2021 legislative agenda, and unanimously entered closed session before approving the January 14, 2021 personnel report 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Amended Agenda, and Amended December 2, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding member Frederick Xavier Ravin III opened the work session and led a moment of silence focused on mental and emotional health. The board added Item 8D for reviewing a draft legislative agenda, approved the amended agenda 7-0 by roll call (moved by Matt Sears, seconded by Natalie Beyer), and approved the December 2, 2020 minutes as amended to fix a name typo on page 10 7-0 by roll call (moved by Beyer, seconded by Dr. Mike Lee).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Read-aloud public comments included concern that remote learning was leaving K-2 students behind (urging the end of Wednesday non-academic schedules), praise from prospective DPS parents for data-driven pandemic decisions, and a proposal to shift the fourth quarter into the summer after an extended spring break.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Design/Construction, DPI Item, Change Order Log, FY19-20 Budget Amendment #4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed four consent items covering elementary school design and construction, a North Carolina DPI item, the DPS design and construction quarterly change order log, and FY2019-20 Budget Amendment #4. Dr. Mike Lee moved and Matt Sears seconded approving the consent agenda as presented, passing 7-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Construction Management at Risk (CM at Risk) for 2020 Capital Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Frederick Davis presented the recommendation to use the Construction Manager at Risk (CM at Risk) delivery method for multiple 2020 capital improvement projects, highlighting how issuing subcontractor RFPs expands MWBE participation and dollar share. Dr. Mike Lee moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded approving CM at Risk, passing 7-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Elementary Design Consultants and $15/Hour Minimum Wage Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk introduced qualifications-based design consultant recommendations from six shortlisted firms for multiple elementary school renovations and additions, ahead of a scheduled $15/hour minimum wage update. Discussion and any action on items 7B and 7C occurred within the truncated middle section of the digest.

agenda_items.title: National Mentoring Month and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after the truncated middle section, board members read aloud resolutions declaring January 2021 National Mentoring Month and celebrating the life and service of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., thanking community advocate Mr. Langley for his leadership. Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded adopting both resolutions together, passing 7-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Postponement of Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Selection Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because the online polling form initially listed only one option, board members consulted board attorney Ken Soo on open-meetings requirements and agreed to extend the application window to January 22 (sending nominees to the board January 25) for a public vote on January 28. Alexandra Valladares moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded postponing the task force vote to January 28, passing 7-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Draft 2021 Legislative Agenda Review, Teacher Diversity Grant, and Follow-Up Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed the draft 2021 legislative agenda to post for public feedback and narrow to five top priorities on January 28, and praised Dr. Nakia Hardy and communications staff for elevating the Teacher Diversity Grant before summarizing follow-up deadlines.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and January 14, 2021 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Alexandra Valladares moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded entering closed session, passing 7-0 by roll call at 01:58:24. Returning to open session at 02:14:32, Natalie Beyer moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded approving the January 14, 2021 personnel report, passing 7-0 by roll call before adjournment.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed 7-0; Personnel report passed 7-0

votes.item_title: Approval of Amended January 14, 2021 Work Session Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 roll call vote (confirmed by Chair Ravin at 00:06:07 after noting his mic was muted during the initial call).
votes.discussion_detail: Matt Sears moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approving the work session agenda with Item 8D added for draft legislative agenda review; presiding member Frederick Xavier Ravin III confirmed his own affirmative vote at 00:06:07 alongside the rest of the board for a 7-0 result.

votes.item_title: Approval of Amended December 2, 2020 Work Session Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: After Jovonia Lewis corrected a name typo on page 10 ('Frederick by your data' to 'Frederick Ravin'), Natalie Beyer moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded approving the amended December 2, 2020 minutes, passing 7-0 by roll call.

votes.item_title: Approval of Construction Management at Risk (CM at Risk) Delivery Method for 2020 Capital Projects
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Frederick Davis's presentation on using CM at Risk to expand MWBE subcontractor access on 2020 capital improvement projects, Dr. Mike Lee moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded approval, passing unanimously by roll call.

votes.item_title: Adoption of National Mentoring Month Declaration and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Resolution
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approving both the January 2021 National Mentoring Month declaration and the resolution honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. together, passing 7-0 unanimously by roll call.

votes.item_title: Motion to Postpone Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Selection Vote to January 28, 2021
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Alexandra Valladares moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded postponing the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force member selection vote to the January 28, 2021 regular board meeting after extending the application deadline to January 22, passing unanimously by roll call.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Alexandra Valladares moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded entering closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda, passing unanimously by roll call.

votes.item_title: Approval of January 14, 2021 Personnel Report
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Returning to open session at 02:14:32, Natalie Beyer moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded approving the January 14, 2021 personnel report, passing unanimously by roll call.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Special Meeting January 7, 2021  5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At a January 7, 2021 specially called meeting presided over by Chair Bettina Umstead—who opened by condemning the January 6 assault on the U.S. Capitol and thanking DPS staff for rapidly distributing classroom processing resources—the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved its agenda 7-0 and received a detailed COVID-19 and vaccine briefing from ABC Science Collaborative physicians Dr. Weber and Dr. Archiboyo. Following discussion of a 92% family survey response rate (including strong interest in in-person services among English learners and students with disabilities) and surging local COVID-19 positivity well above the board's 4% threshold, the board voted 7-0 to remain in Plan C remote learning for the remainder of the 2020-21 school year while directing staff to return with learning and enrichment plans such as Learning Centers and small pods for English learners and exceptional children. The board then voted 7-0 to enter closed session and returned to unanimously approve the January 7, 2021 personnel report 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Statement on U.S. Capitol Events, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the special meeting by condemning the January 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol, thanking communications staff and educators for equipping classrooms with social-emotional and primary-source analysis tools, and leading a moment of silence. The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the meeting agenda 7-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: ABC Science Collaborative Briefing on COVID-19 Trends and Vaccine Rollout
agenda_items.discussion_summary: ABC Science Collaborative physicians Dr. Weber and Dr. Archiboyo briefed the board on surging COVID-19 deaths, mRNA vaccine mechanisms and efficacy (roughly 50% after one dose and full immunity after two doses), clinical trial diversity, ultra-cold storage and English-only state database challenges, and excused employee leave policies for post-vaccination reactions.

agenda_items.title: Family Survey Results and Vote to Remain in Plan C for 2020-21 Academic Year
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after a middle truncation, board members celebrated a 92% family survey participation rate (95% White, 94% Hispanic, 90% Black), noting that 52% of English learners, 46% of students with disabilities, and 43% of AIG students expressed interest in in-person learning. Given high community COVID positivity above the board's 4% benchmark and logistical disruption of switching teachers mid-semester, the board voted unanimously (seconded by Dr. Mike Lee) to remain in Plan C for the 2020-21 academic year with plans for continued Learning Centers and targeted enrichment for EL and EC students, while also welcoming county support toward $15/hour staff pay.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and January 7, 2021 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously voted by roll call to enter closed session, reminding viewers to wear masks, wash hands, and maintain six feet of distance. Returning to open session at 02:40:44, the board unanimously approved the January 7, 2021 personnel report 7-0 by roll call before adjourning.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously; Personnel report passed 7-0

votes.item_title: Approval of January 7, 2021 Special Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 vote; individual mover and seconder not named, and Frederick Xavier Ravin III and Alexandra Valladares fell in a brief omitted gap prior to Jovonia Lewis.
votes.discussion_detail: A board member moved and another seconded approving the special meeting agenda as presented, passing unanimously by roll-call voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion for Durham Public Schools to Remain in Plan C for the 2020-21 Academic Year with Enrichment Plans
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 vote; mover name was garbled in the transcript ('I think said I would make a motion') and Frederick Xavier Ravin III / Alexandra Valladares responses fell in a brief omitted gap prior to Jovonia Lewis.
votes.discussion_detail: Following review of health metrics and the 92% family survey response, a motion was made (seconded by Dr. Mike Lee) that Durham Public Schools remain in Plan C for the 2020-21 academic year with staff returning plans for continued learning and enrichment, passing unanimously by roll call.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 vote; individual mover/seconders not named.
votes.discussion_detail: A board member moved and two members seconded entering closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda, passing unanimously by roll call.

votes.item_title: Approval of January 7, 2021 Personnel Report
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 roll call vote; individual mover and seconder not named.
votes.discussion_detail: Returning to open session at 02:40:44, the board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the January 7, 2021 personnel report by roll call.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session  December 10, 2020  5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Presiding Work Session Chair Matt Sears opened the December 10, 2020 Durham Public Schools Board of Education work session with tributes and a moment of silence for longtime superintendent's assistant Sylvia Rogers and retiring educator/principal Arasi Adkins. After approving the amended agenda (7-0), November 5 minutes (7-0), and consent agenda including instructional assistant laptops (7-0), the board reviewed Strategic Plan Priority 1 updates, rising Durham County COVID-19 metrics (6.3% positivity and red-zone case rates), Plan B readiness dashboards, and spring learning preference canvassing before unanimously voting 7-0 to continue operating DPS Learning Centers through January 29, 2021. On End-of-Course (EOC) and CTE state exams, the board passed an amendment by Alexandra Valladares and Natalie Beyer raising the proposed exam grading floor from 80 to 90 on a 4-3 vote (Ayes: Bettina Umstead, Alexandra Valladares, Natalie Beyer, Matt Sears; Nays: Dr. Mike Lee, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Jovonia Lewis) and then adopted the 90-to-100 grading scale for 2020-21 on a 6-1 vote (Ayes: Bettina Umstead, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Alexandra Valladares, Natalie Beyer, Jovonia Lewis, Matt Sears; Nay: Dr. Mike Lee). The board unanimously approved the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force nomination process (7-0) and then reconsidered its prior athletics vote, passing 4-3 to reopen basketball, cheerleading, and preseason workouts for soccer, lacrosse, and football (Ayes: Bettina Umstead, Dr. Mike Lee, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Jovonia Lewis; Nays: Alexandra Valladares, Natalie Beyer, Matt Sears) before entering closed session (6-0) and unanimously approving the December 10 personnel report (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence for Sylvia Rogers, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Chair Matt Sears called the work session to order and acknowledged interpreters Martha Romo-Giles and Marty Ramirez. Board members and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga shared remarks honoring the late Sylvia Rogers, longtime assistant to three superintendents, followed by a moment of silence and a retirement recognition and plaque presentation for Arasi Adkins.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer requested adding Item 8D to discuss in-person End-of-Course (EOC) testing requirements, and Dr. Mike Lee gave notice that he would offer a motion to reconsider the previous athletics vote after general business. Beyer moved and Lee seconded approval of the agenda as amended.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: William Sudderth read submitted public comments for 30 minutes, with full submissions posted to the DPS website. Comments addressed restarting school athletics, Ignite Online Academy teacher looping, ABC Science Collaborative safety planning, and overwhelmingly urged the board to remain in remote Plan C amid rising COVID-19 transmission.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 5, 2020 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Matt Sears returned to Item 5 on the written agenda for approval of the November 5, 2020 work session minutes. Natalie Beyer identified an erroneous pull quote and timestamp on page 5, which Alexandra Valladares accepted as an amendment to her approval motion.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Instructional Assistant Laptop Purchase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer highlighted Item 7E regarding the purchase of laptop devices for instructional assistants and confirmed with staff that CARES Act flexibility allowed purchasing identical models for all remaining instructional assistants. Alexandra Valladares moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded approval of the six-item consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 1 Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and goal team leads presented updates on Strategic Plan Priority 1 (academic achievement, growth, graduation rate, and personalized technology) while prioritizing student social-emotional well-being under Plan C. Natalie Beyer urged transparent family communication and support resources for disconnected students.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Health Department COVID-19 Data Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Health Department lead nurse Susan Thompson reported worsening local metrics, including over 600 active cases, a 7-day moving average of 112 daily cases, 6.3% weekly test positivity, a red-zone case incidence rate of 29.89 per 100,000, and Durham shifting from yellow to orange on the state alert system. Board members clarified that DPS monitors Durham County Health Department positivity rates (two consecutive weeks below 4%) and seven-day moving averages.

agenda_items.title: Plan B Update, Data Dashboards, and Learning Centers Continuation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Hardy, Matthew Hickson, and Dr. Julie Spencer presented the cross-functional Plan B family canvassing effort (reaching 54-57% response rate toward the December 18 spring preference form deadline), weekly COVID-19 health and operational readiness dashboards, and the ABC Science Collaborative screening app rollout. Staff reported 332 students enrolled in DPS Learning Centers with zero on-site COVID-19 transmission and a projected net deficit of $1,207,888 through January 29, 2021, which finance staff noted would be covered via state hold-harmless cost savings rather than fund balance.

agenda_items.title: In-Person EOC and CTE Testing Requirements and Grading Scale
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following up on Natalie Beyer's added item, Dr. Spencer briefed the board on state EOC/CTE testing rules, extended makeup windows through February 15 and spring, and the district's interim 50-100 exam grading floor. Frederick Xavier Ravin III moved to set an 80-100 scale for 2020-21 EOC and CTE exams; Alexandra Valladares and Natalie Beyer successfully amended the floor to 90-100 (4-3) before the board adopted the 90-100 pandemic grading scale (6-1).

agenda_items.title: Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Nomination Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bettina Umstead presented the application and timeline to fill DPS's five seats on the joint Community Safety and Wellness Task Force (one education seat, two youth seats under age 25, and two at-large seats), with applications due January 4, 2021 and board appointments slated for January 14, 2021. Natalie Beyer moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded approval of the nomination process.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Reconsider Reopening High School Athletics
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded a motion to reconsider the November 19 vote rejecting athletics, proposing to reopen basketball and cheerleading (with January 4 first contests) and preseason workouts for men's soccer, men's and women's lacrosse, and football, while noting swimming lacked a Durham Parks and Recreation indoor facility and field hockey could not be salvaged. Supporters cited principal feedback, strict masking and screening protocols, mental health, and college recruiting equity, while opponents argued surging COVID-19 rates and indoor basketball risks contradicted the district's Plan C safety posture and public sacrifice messaging.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Matt Sears summarized follow-up items regarding moderate dashboard metrics, attendance/grade transparency, and family outreach. The board voted 6-0 (with Alexandra Valladares frozen on video) to enter closed session, then reconvened and unanimously approved the December 10, 2020 personnel report before adjourning.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed 6-0; Personnel report passed 7-0

votes.item_title: Approval of December 10, 2020 Work Session Agenda (as Amended to Add Item 8D on In-Person EOC Testing)
votes.notes: Unanimous roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer requested adding Item 8D to discuss state-mandated in-person EOC testing requirements, and Dr. Mike Lee noted he would bring a standard motion to reconsider a prior vote after general business. The amended agenda passed unanimously by roll call.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 5, 2020 Work Session Minutes (as Amended)
votes.notes: Unanimous roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Alexandra Valladares moved approval of the November 5, 2020 minutes and accepted Natalie Beyer's friendly amendment to delete an erroneous pull quote and timestamp on page 5, seconded by Bettina Umstead.

votes.item_title: Continuation of DPS Learning Centers Through January 29, 2021
votes.notes: Unanimous roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff recommended continuing DPS Learning Centers (serving 332 enrolled students with a waitlist under 100 and zero on-site transmission) through January 29, 2021, at a cumulative net cost of $1,207,888 covered via state hold-harmless cost savings. Frederick Xavier Ravin III moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval.

votes.item_title: Amendment to EOC/CTE Grading Scale Motion (Raising Floor from 80 to 90)
votes.notes: Split 4-3 roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Alexandra Valladares proposed amending Frederick Xavier Ravin III's 80-to-100 grading scale motion to set the floor at 90-to-100 to protect students amid pandemic learning disruptions. Ravin expressed concern about optics of a single-letter-grade scale, and Legal Counsel Ken Soo clarified that a second by Natalie Beyer placed the amendment before the board for a vote.

votes.item_title: Adoption of 90-to-100 Grading Scale for State-Required EOC and CTE Pathway Exams (2020-21)
votes.notes: Split 6-1 roll call vote on main motion as amended.
votes.discussion_detail: Board members clarified that the 90-to-100 scale applies only to state-mandated EOC and CTE post-assessments for the 2020-21 school year (fall and spring windows, including students who take an incomplete and postpone testing) and that administration would communicate the options immediately to families.

votes.item_title: Approval of Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Nomination Process
votes.notes: Unanimous roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Bettina Umstead presented the application form and timeline (due January 4, 2021; appointments January 14, 2021) for DPS's five seats on the joint task force. Natalie Beyer inquired about minimum age for the youth seats and agreed to use board discretion during selection.

votes.item_title: Reconsideration and Approval of Reopening High School Athletics (Basketball, Cheerleading, and Preseason Workouts for Soccer, Lacrosse, and Football)
votes.notes: Split 4-3 roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Mike Lee brought back the athletics reopening proposal rejected on November 19, limiting it to basketball and cheerleading seasons plus preseason workouts for men's soccer, men's and women's lacrosse, and football (excluding swimming due to lack of facility and field hockey). Supporters emphasized high school principals' advocacy, strict masking and screening protocols, mental health, and college recruiting equity, while opponents warned of worsening COVID-19 spread and indoor basketball risk.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Passed 6-0 with Alexandra Valladares disconnected/frozen.
votes.discussion_detail: The board voted to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda; Alexandra Valladares's video connection froze during the roll call.

votes.item_title: Approval of December 10, 2020 Personnel Report
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Frederick Xavier Ravin III also seconded.
votes.discussion_detail: Upon returning to open session, the board unanimously approved the December 10, 2020 personnel report recommended by Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session  December 10, 2020  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: EOC and CTE Exam Grading Scale Floor (80-100 vs. 90-100)
disagreements.summary: Board members split 4-3 over whether to amend the proposed 80-to-100 pandemic grading scale floor for state-mandated EOC and CTE exams to 90-to-100, and then voted 6-1 to adopt the 90-to-100 scale.
disagreements.side_a_position: Raise the minimum exam score floor to 90-to-100 to give students maximum grade protection during remote pandemic learning and encourage families who feel unsafe testing in person to postpone.
side_a_arguments: Pandemic learning disruptions are unprecedented and students deserve the strongest possible protection on exams weighted at 20% of course grades.
With a 90-to-100 scale, students who postpone testing with an incomplete until spring will not be penalized academically for prioritizing safety.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep the floor at 80-to-100 to preserve a two-letter-grade range (A and B) and avoid the optics of a single-grade scale.
side_b_arguments: A 90-to-100 scale leaves only a single letter grade (A), creating poor optics compared to an 80-to-100 range with As and Bs.
An 80-to-100 floor already substantially mitigates potential grade loss for students who postpone testing until spring.
disagreements.resolution: The amendment to adopt a 90-to-100 scale passed 4-3, and the final amended motion passed 6-1 with only Dr. Mike Lee voting no.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session  December 10, 2020  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Reconsideration of Reopening High School Athletics During COVID-19 Surge
disagreements.summary: Following a reconsideration motion by Dr. Mike Lee, the board split 4-3 to approve reopening basketball, cheerleading, and preseason workouts for soccer, lacrosse, and football despite rising county COVID-19 transmission.
disagreements.side_a_position: Reopen approved winter sports and spring preseason workouts under strict masking, screening, and no-spectator protocols so student-athletes do not lose scholarships, mental health, or multiple seasons.
side_a_arguments: Overwhelming emails from families and direct outreach from high school principals urged restoring athletic opportunities, noting neighboring districts were already playing.
Losing senior or consecutive seasons harms student-athletes' mental health and college recruiting prospects, especially for students of color.
Participation is voluntary for families and governed by mandatory masking during play, parent safety meetings, and health department tracking.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep sports paused while community COVID-19 rates are worse than in November and students remain out of classrooms under Plan C.
side_b_arguments: Durham's COVID-19 metrics (6.3% positivity, 29.89 cases per 100,000) are substantially worse than when the board rejected athletics on November 19.
Indoor close-contact basketball poses high transmission risk and contradicts asking families to sacrifice holiday gatherings and keeping classrooms closed.
Reopening sports privileges athletics while arts, culinary, and hands-on CTE students remain deprived of in-person workshops.
disagreements.resolution: The motion to reopen basketball, cheerleading, and preseason workouts for soccer, lacrosse, and football passed 4-3.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting  November 19, 2020  6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead presided over the November 19, 2020 Durham Public Schools Board of Education meeting, opening with celebrations for City of Medicine Academy and an urgent recommendation from Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga to give families a second-semester in-person option while warning of multi-year pandemic learning loss. After unanimously approving the amended agenda (7-0), October 22 minutes (7-0), posting 447 written public comments online rather than reading them aloud (7-0), the consent agenda (7-0), and a Policy 7130 licensure amendment (7-0), the board held an intense debate over Plan B reopening. Matt Sears's motion to continue community planning without approving Plan B as presented was announced as failing by Chair Umstead despite the transcript recording Jovonia Lewis, Natalie Beyer, Matt Sears, and Alexandra Valladares voting Yes against Dr. Mike Lee, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, and Bettina Umstead voting No; the board then adopted Dr. Mike Lee's motion as amended by Frederick Xavier Ravin III to plan toward a January 21/25 opt-in Plan B reopening contingent on Durham's COVID-19 positivity rate remaining below 4% for two consecutive weeks on an announced 4-3 vote (Ayes in transcript: Jovonia Lewis, Dr. Mike Lee, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Bettina Umstead, with Natalie Beyer's voice transcribed as 'Yeah'; Nays: Matt Sears, Alexandra Valladares, plus a third Nay reflected in the Chair's announced 4-3 tally). Finally, the board rejected reopening basketball, cheerleading, field hockey, lacrosse, soccer, and football by a 3-4 vote (Ayes: Jovonia Lewis, Dr. Mike Lee, Frederick Xavier Ravin III; Nays: Natalie Beyer, Matt Sears, Alexandra Valladares, Bettina Umstead), unanimously adopted a resolution seeking state and federal high-stakes testing waivers (7-0), and approved the November 19 personnel report (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the meeting and led a moment of silence reflecting on holiday stress, the COVID-19 pandemic, and local gun violence. Principal Dr. Jackie Tobias introduced City of Medicine Academy senior Sophia Lazo as November Student of the Month and recognized science teacher Mr. Hewitt.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga warned that over 50% of students enter kindergarten below grade level and that prolonged virtual learning under Plan C risks long-term academic recovery. He recommended offering families a safe, phased in-person choice for second semester rather than committing to Plan C for the rest of the year.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval of October 22, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board amended the agenda to add a resolution requesting state and federal waivers from high-stakes testing during COVID-19 prior to closed session, passing the amended agenda unanimously (7-0). The board then unanimously approved the October 22, 2020 meeting minutes (7-0).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment Handling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: William Sudderth reported 447 written public comments received and posted to the DPS website. With legal counsel confirming statutory compliance because oral/earlier public comment had been provided that month, Jovonia Lewis moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded posting the 447 comments online without reading them aloud.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Policy 7130 Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the consent agenda covering fall cleanup policies, Brogden Middle School freezer/cooler replacement, instructional assistant laptops, Gaggle Safety, and Learning A-Z (7-0). Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni and Dr. Dietrich Danner then presented a state-mandated licensure language amendment to Policy 7130, which passed unanimously with waiver of second reading (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Plan B Second-Semester Reopening Recommendation and Threshold Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration presented a detailed Plan B proposal beginning second semester (targeting January 21) for elementary students and self-contained EC classes while keeping middle and high school in Plan C, detailing bus capacity limits, Ignite re-enrollment, teacher accommodation requests (700 total, 171 K-5 teachers), and readiness dashboards. Matt Sears's motion to direct continued community planning without approving Plan B was announced as failed by Chair Umstead; the board then adopted Dr. Mike Lee's motion as amended by Frederick Xavier Ravin III to authorize Plan B planning as an opt-in model (Plan C default) contingent on county COVID-19 positivity staying below 4% for at least two weeks and a January 7 board review.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Sears motion announced failed 3-4; Amended Lee/Ravin motion passed 4-3

agenda_items.title: Athletics Reopening Recommendation (Winter and Spring Contact Sports)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration and Athletic Director David Hackney sought clearance to begin basketball, cheerleading, and field hockey along with off-season skill-building for men's soccer, men's and women's lacrosse, and football. Dr. Mike Lee moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded approval, while Natalie Beyer questioned compliance with Durham's 10-person gathering limits and Matt Sears and Bettina Umstead voted no, defeating the motion 3-4.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Requesting State and Federal Waivers from High-Stakes Testing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer read a resolution drafted in response to a teacher petition urging North Carolina and the U.S. Department of Education (under both the Trump and incoming Biden administrations) to waive EOC and standardized high-stakes testing requirements during virtual instruction and rising COVID-19 rates. Matt Sears moved and Natalie Beyer seconded adoption, and the board agreed to forward the resolution to the Durham legislative delegation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Chair Umstead urged the public to mask, distance, and keep holiday gatherings within households, the board unanimously entered closed session (7-0). Upon reconvening in open session, the board unanimously approved the November 19, 2020 personnel report (7-0) and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed 7-0; Personnel report passed 7-0

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.

votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Mike Lee moved to authorize planning toward a January 21 Plan B target with a January 7 review meeting, and accepted Frederick Xavier Ravin III's friendly amendment requiring families to opt in to physical school (keeping Plan C virtual as the default) and requiring the estimated COVID-19 positivity rate to fall below 4% and remain below 4% for at least two consecutive weeks (opening no earlier than January 21/25).

Natalie Beyer questioned compliance with Durham's 10-person indoor gathering restriction, and four members voted no.

votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer introduced and read aloud a resolution requesting North Carolina apply to the U.S. Department of Education under both the Trump and Biden administrations for waivers from EOC and all other high-stakes standardized assessments during the pandemic.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting  November 19, 2020  6:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Plan B Second-Semester Reopening Framework, Opt-In Default, and <4% Positivity Threshold
disagreements.summary: The board divided over whether to defer approval of Plan B for continued community planning or authorize January 21/25 planning under an opt-in model gated by a sustained <4% COVID-19 positivity threshold.
disagreements.side_a_position: Authorize administration to plan toward a January 21/25 second-semester Plan B reopening under an opt-in default, contingent on county positivity remaining below 4% for at least two consecutive weeks.
side_a_arguments: Staff need a target date and operational authorization now to hire, schedule, and prepare logistics if conditions improve.
Switching to an opt-in model keeps Plan C as the default for most families while reserving limited in-person seats for vulnerable and EC students who need them.
Requiring two consecutive weeks below 4% positivity ensures the district will not reopen during a surge.
disagreements.side_b_position: Do not approve a target date or metric-triggered Plan B yet; prioritize multilingual outreach, community input, and wait until infection curves actually decline.
side_b_arguments: Community COVID-19 infection curves are surging, making it premature to commit to a specific reopening date or fixed percentage threshold.
Board materials and Plan B details have not yet been fully translated and communicated across all languages spoken by DPS families.
Staffing risks and the lack of clear cost-benefit justification for hybrid instruction require further refinement before board approval.
disagreements.resolution: Matt Sears's deferral motion was announced as failed by Chair Umstead; Dr. Mike Lee's motion incorporating Frederick Xavier Ravin III's opt-in and <4% positivity amendment passed on an announced 4-3 roll call vote (with Natalie Beyer having backed Sears's deferral motion and urged tabling, while the Chair announced 4-3).

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting  November 19, 2020  6:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Reopening Winter and Contact High School Athletics
disagreements.summary: Board members split 3-4 on whether to approve starting winter basketball, cheerleading, field hockey, and off-season workouts for lacrosse, soccer, and football.
disagreements.side_a_position: Allow voluntary student-athlete participation under NCHSAA safety protocols and parent waivers to support student mental health, academic motivation, and athletic development.
side_a_arguments: Following NCHSAA guidelines, screenings, and parent risk disclosures provides transparency and choice for families.
Athletics motivate academic engagement and provide college pathway opportunities.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject expanding high school athletics while indoor gathering limits are restricted and in-person classroom instruction remains closed.
side_b_arguments: Indoor contact sports conflict with Durham's 10-person gathering limit and ongoing COVID-19 spread.
Opening sports while classrooms remain closed sends troubling optics and raises safety and liability concerns.
disagreements.resolution: The motion to approve the athletics reopening plan failed 3-4.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham Board of County Commissioners Joint Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead presided over the November 17, 2020 joint meeting of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education and the Durham Board of County Commissioners. The two boards unanimously approved prior joint meeting minutes and the 2021 quarterly joint meeting calendar, while receiving budget and revenue updates from County Budget Director Keith Lane and DPS CFO Paul LeSieur/Alex Modesto detailing the first-year $1.9 million phase-in toward a $15/hour classified minimum wage ($14/hour in FY21) and warning of COVID-19 revenue uncertainty, $3.83 million in DPS fund balance usage, and rising learning center, connectivity, and HEPA filter expenses. DPS leadership briefed commissioners on the draft second-semester Plan B reopening framework and readiness dashboards, and Dr. Julius Monk reviewed major capital projects including Northern High School (summer 2021 construction), Elementary School F, six elementary renovations, and the planned 2022 bond/LOBS financing strategy. County and Durham Children's Initiative staff concluded with updates on the Early Childhood Action Plan and Durham Pre-K (supporting 441 local-dollar-braided seats) ahead of February 2021 budget coordination.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Review, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the joint BOE-BOCC meeting to order and confirmed no agenda changes were needed. Present BOCC Commissioners (Howerton, Jacobs, Carter) and DPS Board Members (Ravin, Beyer, Lewis, Umstead) unanimously approved the prior joint meeting minutes by roll call.

agenda_items.title: FY 2020-21 Budget Follow-Up and $15/Hour Minimum Wage Phase-In
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Budget Director Keith Lane reviewed the county's $1.9 million FY21 allocation toward a two-year phase-in of DPS's $15/hour classified wage request (bringing minimum pay to ~$14/hour, leaving $1,907,000 needed for full implementation) while cautioning that property tax and sales tax collections remained uncertain until January 2021 and county vacant positions were frozen. DPS board members and commissioners discussed whether county fund balance reserves could accelerate full $15/hour funding in January 2021 for essential pandemic workers.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Learning and Plan B Reopening Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Dr. Julie Spencer presented DPS's draft second-semester Plan B framework and upcoming weekly health and site-readiness dashboards. Commissioners praised the depth of planning and expressed commitment to supporting whichever instructional decision the school board makes.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Projects and 2022 Bond/LOBS Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk updated both boards on the $500 million 10-year capital commitment, noting Northern High School construction starts in summer 2021, Elementary School F design negotiations with a Durham minority-owned firm are underway, six elementary school renovations are in RFQ review for 2023 completion, and high school theater lighting is out for bid. Natalie Beyer pressed for a 2022 GO bond to address deferred HVAC, roof, and Jordan High School needs, and Keith Lane and county staff affirmed commitment to meeting the CIP schedule through LOBS and a planned 2022 bond referendum.

agenda_items.title: DPS COVID-19 Relief Funding, Connectivity, and Budget Risks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Paul LeSieur and Alex Modesto detailed state ADM hold-harmless protection at 33,368 students (versus 31,603 actual enrollment), CARES Act ($11.9M) and Coronavirus Relief Fund allocations expiring December 30, 2020, and looming FY22 fiscal cliffs including $2.6 million in annual hotspot connectivity and $2.5 million in annual 1:1 device refresh costs alongside $1.5 million in Learning Center deficits and $800,000 in HEPA filtration. Frederick Xavier Ravin III suggested exploring remaining CRF Wi-Fi equipment funds for community Wi-Fi extenders, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs noted the county's northern broadband study.

agenda_items.title: Early Childhood Action Plan and Durham Pre-K Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Early Childhood Coordinator Katie Lender, DCI's David Reese, and Linda Chappelle presented progress on the county's Early Childhood Action Plan (high-level recommendations due February/March, final plan in June) and Durham Pre-K. Chappelle reported local dollars were supporting 441 braided Pre-K seats (136 fully locally funded) and expressed hope for additional state Leandro Pre-K funding.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 2021 Joint Meeting Schedule and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The boards unanimously approved the 2021 quarterly joint meeting calendar with locations pending health guidance. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs flagged that the gap between February and May meetings might require an interim budget coordination session, which Chair Umstead welcomed, and Alexandra Valladares asked the county to include DPS in future environmental and building sustainability contracts.

votes.item_title: Approval of Joint BOE-BOCC Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint board roll call: 4 DPS members present (Ravin, Beyer, Lewis, Umstead) voted Yes; BOCC Commissioners Jacobs and Carter (and Howerton called) voted Yes; Dr. Mike Lee, Matt Sears, and Alexandra Valladares not recorded in this early roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Bettina Umstead called the roll of present BOCC commissioners (Jacobs, Carter; Howerton noted on screen) and DPS school board members (Ravin, Beyer, Lewis, Umstead) to approve the prior joint meeting minutes.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2021 Joint BOE-BOCC Quarterly Meeting Schedule
votes.notes: Joint board roll call: DPS members Lewis, Beyer, Ravin, and Umstead voted Aye; BOCC Commissioners Jacobs, Howerton, and Carter voted Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved four quarterly joint meetings for 2021 with physical or virtual locations pending health and safety guidance.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session November 5, 2020  5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Presiding Work Session Chair Natalie Beyer led the November 5, 2020 Durham Public Schools Board of Education work session through a heavy slate of policy, facilities, budget, and pandemic readiness actions. The board unanimously approved the amended agenda (7-0), October 8 minutes (7-0), consent agenda including a trauma-informed leadership teams contract (7-0), and Policy 5110 (7-0), while advancing first-reading cleanup policies including a new teacher crowdfunding policy (7360/85) by a 6-1 vote (Ayes: Bettina Umstead, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Dr. Mike Lee, Jovonia Lewis, Alexandra Valladares, Matt Sears; Nay: Natalie Beyer, who sought teacher feedback first). The board unanimously authorized ranked design contract negotiations with Evoke Studio Architecture for Elementary School F (7-0), approved $731,805 in wages for 175 temporary part-time custodians for Plan B disinfecting (7-0), approved the Snow Hill Road Park/Lucas Middle School property exchange and interlocal agreement with the City of Durham (7-0), adopted the FY 2020-21 budget resolution (7-0), and approved purchasing 373 HEPA air purifiers from Home Depot for $228,154.78 (7-0). On an emergency agenda item, the board approved a Memorandum of Understanding with the Duke ABC Science Collaborative for a COVID-19 symptom-screening app on a 4-3 vote (Ayes: Dr. Mike Lee, Bettina Umstead, Jovonia Lewis, Frederick Xavier Ravin III; Nays: Alexandra Valladares, Matt Sears, Natalie Beyer) after intense debate over research ties, community trust, and alternative apps like Greenlight Ed, before unanimously approving all 53 School Improvement Plans (7-0), the closed-session personnel report (7-0), and school safety plans (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Review, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Chair Natalie Beyer opened the work session, acknowledged interpreters Martha Romo-Giles and Marty Ramirez, and led a moment of silence during election week. The board unanimously added two emergency items (air filter purchase and ABC Science Collaborative MOU) to the agenda (7-0) and approved the October 8, 2020 work session minutes (7-0).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Submitted public comments posted on the DPS website were read aloud, featuring calls from parents and athletes to resume high school sports, criticism of reopening pressures, and appeals to follow ABC Science Collaborative data-driven guidance on safe in-person instruction.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the two-item consent agenda covering the renaming/renumbering of policies 3000, 3227, 4303, and 3020 and a 2020 trauma-informed leadership teams contract with the Center for Child and Family Health for every elementary school.

agenda_items.title: Chief of Staff: Policy 5110 (Third Reading) and Cleanup Policies (First Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented Policy 5110 (Relationship with County Commissioners) on third reading with historical revisions drafted with Dr. Spencer, which passed unanimously (7-0). She then presented first-reading cleanup policies including Policy 3100 (culturally responsive curriculum), Policy 4304 (seclusion and restraint), and a new crowdfunding policy (7360/85) requiring principal approval up to $5,000 and superintendent approval up to $25,000; Natalie Beyer objected to advancing crowdfunding without teacher input, and the slate passed 6-1.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Elementary School F Design Consultant Selection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk and Fred Davis presented the RFQ selection process under Policy 9110 for the $49 million, 800-student Elementary School F (adjacent to Hope Valley Farms, equipped with Pre-K classrooms and sustainability oversight), ranking Evoke Studio Architecture, Little, and Moseley as finalists. The board unanimously authorized staff to negotiate a design contract in ranked order starting with Durham-based Black-owned firm Evoke Studio Architecture.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Plan B Enhanced Disinfecting Custodial Staffing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Travis Anderson presented Plan B enhanced disinfecting requirements, comparing $3 million+ in contracted services against $731,805 in wages to hire 175 temporary 10-month part-time custodians at $15/hour (20 hours/week, without benefits), funded via utility and operational savings. Jovonia Lewis moved and Alexandra Valladares seconded approval.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Snow Hill Road Park / Lucas Middle School Property Exchange
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk and Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented a property exchange and interlocal agreement with the City of Durham under G.S. 160A-274 and 160A-461 formalizing a decade-long handshake arrangement on shared athletic fields and parcel boundaries at Lucas Middle School and Snow Hill Road Park. Alexandra Valladares moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded approval.

agenda_items.title: FY 2020-21 Budget Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Paul LeSieur and Alex Modesto presented the annual balanced budget resolution under G.S. 115C-425, detailing CARES Act and state relief constraints, $28.2 million in local charter school pass-throughs (39% of new county funding), $1 million private school set-aside, and Plan B reopening cost risks. Following discussion of charter school fiscal impacts, $15/hour classified pay mid-year advocacy, and hazard pay, the board unanimously adopted the budget resolution.

agenda_items.title: Purchase of 373 HEPA Air Purifiers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk recommended an urgent $228,154.78 purchase of 373 HEPA air purifiers from Home Depot (using CARES Act and local funds) for Pre-K classrooms, self-contained EC rooms, nurses' offices, and isolation rooms. Dr. Mike Lee moved and Frederick Xavier Ravin III seconded approval.

agenda_items.title: MOU with Duke ABC Science Collaborative for Symptom-Screening App
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration and legal counsel presented a Data Use Agreement and MOU with the Duke ABC Science Collaborative to host a COVID-19 symptom-screening app for DPS staff and students, emphasizing that DPS retains ownership of all data and families must separately opt in and sign parental consent for any research.
