disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session November 5, 2020  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Advancing Teacher Crowdfunding Policy (7360/85) on First Reading Without Teacher Input
disagreements.summary: The board split 6-1 on advancing first-reading cleanup policies that included a new policy requiring principal approval for teacher crowdfunding campaigns up to $5,000 and superintendent approval up to $25,000.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the cleanup policy batch including Policy 7360/85 on first reading to promote equity, asset accountability, and visibility into unmet classroom needs, while collecting teacher feedback before or after second reading.
side_a_arguments: The $5,000 principal and $25,000 superintendent thresholds are high enough to avoid burdening routine classroom campaigns.
Tracking crowdfunding helps the district identify unmet school needs and establish clear property ownership rules.
disagreements.side_b_position: Pull the crowdfunding policy before advancing so teachers can review and provide input on how principal-permission rules affect their practice.
side_b_arguments: Durham teachers frequently rely on crowdfunding and a teacher already messaged asking to give feedback.
Requiring principal sign-off even for small $100 music or classroom requests represents a major procedural shift that warrants teacher engagement first.
disagreements.resolution: The motion to advance the cleanup policies to second reading passed 6-1 with Natalie Beyer voting no.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session November 5, 2020  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Duke ABC Science Collaborative Symptom-Screening App MOU vs. Independent Service App
disagreements.summary: The board split 4-3 to approve an emergency MOU with the Duke ABC Science Collaborative for a COVID-19 symptom-screening app after sharp debate over research ties, short notice, and alternative local apps.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the vetted Duke ABC Science Collaborative MOU immediately so staff and learning center families can begin training on a free, FERPA-compliant symptom checker owned by DPS.
side_a_arguments: DPS retains ownership of all student data, researchers cannot access data without DPS direction, and families must separately opt in and sign parental consent for research.
Duke IRB oversight and legal vetting by Tanya Giovanni and Dr. Julie Spencer provide stronger data protection than commercial vendors, and Dr. Sendak's alternative app carried added cost.
Learning centers and staff need the screening tool next week ahead of potential Plan B reopening.
disagreements.side_b_position: Table or delay the emergency MOU to allow public review, community trust-building, and exploration of an independent service-oriented app (such as Greenlight Ed / Dr. Mark Sendak's team) or joint collaboration.
side_b_arguments: The MOU was added at the last minute without being posted in the public packet or reviewed with families.
Deploying an app built by a medical research team triggers legitimate historical distrust in communities of color and Latinx communities, where ABC webinars had limited public access.

Greenlight Ed / Dr. Sendak's Pandemic Response Network team is already used at Student U and a Durham charter school, partners with community health workers, and is not tied to an active research study.
disagreements.resolution: The motion to approve the ABC Science Collaborative MOU passed 4-3.

meetings.executive_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead presided over the October 22, 2020 Durham Public Schools Board of Education monthly meeting, opening with a moment of silence for longtime Hillside High School band director Clark Edgerton Jr., student and staff celebrations, and updates from Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga on Wellness Wednesdays and parent academies. After approving the agenda (7-0) and amending the September 24 minutes to record Alexandra Valladares's abstention as a 7-0 affirmative vote under board policy (7-0), the board heard 44 public comments and a comprehensive presentation from the City of Durham Racial Equity Task Force (including former Superior Court Judge Elaine O'Neal, Jamal Moss, Howard Martin, Dan McKinney, Vanessa Hines, Katie Ingle-Ngola, and James Chavis) urging trauma-informed investments, SRO divestment, voting student board seats, culturally relevant curricula, and universal Pre-K. The board approved the consent agenda (6-0 with Valladares temporarily disconnected) and second-reading policies (6-0), and then voted 5-2 to reopen high school athletics beginning with volleyball and cross country under no-spectator NCHSAA protocols (Ayes: Dr. Mike Lee, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Jovonia Lewis, Alexandra Valladares, Bettina Umstead; Nays: Matt Sears, Natalie Beyer). Following closed session, the board unanimously approved the October 22 personnel report (7-0).

Recommendations covered trauma-informed schools and a 1:250 counselor ratio, preparing for post-moratorium evictions, divesting from SROs in favor of wraparound services, creating full voting student board seats, racial equity report cards, culturally relevant curriculum, diverse teacher recruitment, and universal pre-K access.

disagreements.issue: Reopening High School Athletics (Volleyball and Cross Country) During Virtual Plan C Instruction
disagreements.summary: The board voted 5-2 to reopen cross country and volleyball without spectators under NCHSAA protocols over objections from two members regarding COVID-19 risk, liability waivers, and opening sports while classrooms remain closed.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve reopening cross country and volleyball with no spectators, transparent risk communication, and strict NCHSAA mitigation protocols as an optional opportunity for students.
side_a_arguments: Cross country and volleyball are lower-risk sports with extensive screening, facility cleaning, and medical return-to-play safeguards.
Participation is voluntary for parents and students, and requiring face masks during competition further minimizes risk.
Sports support students' social-emotional well-being during remote learning.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep athletics closed while school buildings remain closed under Plan C due to district-sanctioned COVID-19 risk, waiver concerns, and conflicting optics.
side_b_arguments: Sanctioning extracurricular athletics while keeping classroom instruction virtual sends mixed messages like reopening bars before schools.
District legal liability and asking parents to sign waivers raise unresolved concerns when indoor volleyball carries aerosol risk.
disagreements.resolution: The motion to approve the athletics reopening plan starting with cross country and volleyball passed 5-2.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk, Jim Keaton, and Alex Modesto reported School Nutrition had reached 5,780 daily breakfasts and lunches via bus routes and home delivery, needing 8,200 daily meals by mid-October to eliminate a $300,000/month deficit. Dr. Monk then presented the lowest responsive bid of $22,830,000 from Montieth Construction (11.94% HUB participation; April 1, 2022 completion) for Elementary School C on Scott King Road, which the board approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: DPS Learning Centers Site Consolidation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy reported 247 students enrolled across six Learning Centers (208 free), generating a three-week deficit of $238,098 and a projected $2.86 million annual shortfall. Following board feedback questioning Carrington Middle School's northern location relative to Shepard and Githens, the board unanimously approved consolidating from six sites down to three or four sites pending Hope Learning Center coordination.

agenda_items.title: Virtual Learning Survey Results and Second-Quarter Plan C Decision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julie Spencer presented September survey results from families, staff, and students, Dr. Hardy outlined Wellness Wednesdays and Plan C adjustments, and Superintendent Dr. Mubenga recommended staying in Plan C through the end of the first semester to prepare a stronger Plan B. Matt Sears moved and Natalie Beyer seconded staying in Plan C for the second quarter, passing 6-1 over Jovonia Lewis's opposition seeking a shorter 4-week pause and phased reopening for EC and K-2 students.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session, Personnel Report, and Superintendent Contract Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously entered closed session including discussion of Wendell Tabb v. DPS BOE (7-0). Upon reconvening, the board approved the September 24 personnel report 6-0-1 (with Alexandra Valladares abstaining, later recorded as 7-0 under board policy) and unanimously voted to extend Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's contract through June 30, 2024 (7-0).

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting September 24,  2020  6:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Duration of Plan C Remote Learning Extension (Full Second Quarter vs. Four-Week Phased Review)
disagreements.summary: The board voted 6-1 to stay in Plan C through the second nine weeks, with Jovonia Lewis dissenting in favor of a shorter four-week extension and a phased-in Plan B option for Exceptional Children and K-2 students prior to January.
disagreements.side_a_position: Remain in remote Plan C for the entire second nine weeks (first semester) while continuing to build safety plans, Ignite capacity, and teacher readiness for a possible January Plan B.
side_a_arguments: Teachers and families need predictability and adequate preparation time rather than mid-quarter schedule disruptions.
With roughly 20% of teachers expressing readiness and rising second-wave risks, large districts should be observed before transitioning.
The board retains authority to revisit phasing in smaller high-need groups if conditions and plans mature.
disagreements.side_b_position: Limit the Plan C extension to four weeks (after the initial nine weeks) and develop an earlier phased-in Plan B option in November for EC self-contained and K-2 students.
side_b_arguments: A blanket second-quarter Plan C commitment leaves behind the most vulnerable students, particularly EC self-contained and early elementary learners.
A four-week checkpoint would force rapid development of psychological safety and small-group in-person options before January.
disagreements.resolution: The motion to remain in Plan C for the second nine weeks passed 6-1 with Jovonia Lewis voting no.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session September 10,  2020  5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Presiding Work Session Chair Jovonia Lewis opened the September 10, 2020 Durham Public Schools Board of Education work session with the swearing-in of newly appointed Consolidated District B member Frederick Xavier Ravin III by Judge Brian Hart. The board unanimously approved the amended agenda (7-0), consent agenda excluding Item C (7-0), the pulled Gaia Global Technologies construction program management software contract (7-0), and amended Title IX interim policies (7-0), while voting 6-1 to amend the agenda to hear an immediate Title I funding update (Ayes: Natalie Beyer, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Alexandra Valladares, Matt Sears, Bettina Umstead, Jovonia Lewis; Nay: Dr. Mike Lee). Later in the evening, the board heard a 7:00 PM COVID-19 data presentation from medical advisors and Nurse Howard (noting 27704, 27703, and 27701 zip code case rates and low secondary school transmission where masking is enforced), reviewed extensive Plan C remote learning, EC, ESL, arts, and student support operations—including state ADM hold-harmless enrollment protections at 33,348 students—and approved the September 10 personnel report unanimously (7-0) following closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Oath of Office for Frederick Xavier Ravin III
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Chair Jovonia Lewis observed a moment of silence for World Suicide Prevention Day and pregnancy-related deaths. Chair Bettina Umstead introduced Frederick Xavier Ravin III, and Judge Brian Hart administered the oath of office for the Consolidated District B seat.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the agenda as amended to take up the COVID-19 data update with medical advisors at 7:00 PM (7-0). Public comments addressed correcting virtual attendance errors at Githens, keeping student safety over reopening amid HVAC limitations, mental health impacts of virtual learning, and pass-fail grading.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda, Gaia Global Technologies Contract, and Title I Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Frederick Xavier Ravin III pulled Item C—the three-year Gaia Global Technologies construction program management software SaaS agreement—to ask about capital vs. operational funding after year three and prorating the 2.5-month term gap ending June 30, 2023. The board approved the remaining consent items (7-0), then approved the Gaia contract (7-0), and voted 6-1 on Alexandra Valladares's motion (seconded by Ravin, with Dr. Mike Lee voting no) to add an immediate Title I federal funding presentation by Dr. Danner.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consent 7-0; Gaia contract 7-0; Title I agenda amendment 6-1

agenda_items.title: Chief of Staff: Interim Title IX Policies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented amended interim Title IX policies for approval, noting the Title IX task force would continue bringing forward additional local protections. Natalie Beyer moved and Alexandra Valladares seconded approval.

agenda_items.title: Plan C Remote Learning Implementation Update (Part 1 & Part 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a National Arts in Education Week resolution reading, Dr. Nakia Hardy and instructional/student services leaders presented comprehensive updates on Plan C implementation since August 17, covering social-emotional learning hubs, EC and IEP accommodations, ESL and Multilingual Resource Center supports, Zoombombing emotional support, AIG Learning Labs, attendance tracking, and state ADM hold-harmless funding at 33,348 students.

agenda_items.title: Durham COVID-19 Data Update with Medical Advisors
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At 7:00 PM, the board paused the Plan C presentation for the COVID-19 data update with medical advisors and lead nurse Howard, reviewing zip-code case disparities (highest rates in 27704, 27703, and 27701) and evidence from districts operating with minimal secondary transmission alongside board questions on monitoring and detailed reopening criteria.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After follow-up summaries, the board unanimously entered closed session (7-0), reconvened in open session, and unanimously approved the September 10, 2020 personnel report (7-0) before adjourning.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session September 10,  2020  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Adding a Title I Federal Funding Update to the Approved Agenda
disagreements.summary: The board voted 6-1 to amend its already-approved agenda to hear an immediate 10-minute presentation on Title I school funding allocations, with Dr. Mike Lee voting no.
disagreements.side_a_position: Amend the agenda immediately to provide a public Title I funding update so families and community members can understand how federal Title I dollars are distributed across DPS schools.
side_a_arguments: Community members frequently ask how federal Title I funds are allocated to schools.
Presenting the Title I plan publicly increases transparency rather than leaving it solely on consent.
disagreements.side_b_position: Decline to amend the already-approved agenda mid-meeting.
side_b_arguments: Voted no during the procedural roll call after the agenda and consent items had already been adopted.
disagreements.resolution: The motion passed 6-1 and Dr. Hardy and Dr. Danner delivered the Title I update.
